#167722. Breaking: GTA 6 vault: How to open them during big bank jobs

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1150 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pcgamer ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: GTA 6 vault: How to open them during big bank jobs

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1150 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opening a GTA 6 bank vault is one of the best ways to make off with a big score during a robbery, with potentially $100,000 or more in bills and valuables from a single heist.
  • But those huge bank vault doors are completely impenetrable, and confusingly, even after you've learned how to drill into a vault as part of a Chapter 3 story mission, you still won't be able to open vault doors in open world bank robberies.
  • It has been revealed that here's the trick: you've got to get someone to open bank vault doors for you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opening a GTA 6 bank vault is one of the best ways to make off with a big score during a robbery, with potentially $100,000 or more in bills and valuables from a single heist.

But those huge bank vault doors are completely impenetrable, and confusingly, even after you've learned how to drill into a vault as part of a Chapter 3 story mission, you still won't be able to open vault doors in open world bank robberies.

It has been revealed that here's the trick: you've got to get someone to open bank vault doors for you. Only then can you steal all that sweet cash.

Your GTA 6 fence, Yasmani, will begin offering you tips once you start selling him stolen goods in Chapter 3: jewelry store heists targeting specific items and which ATM jobs have the most cash, for example. These are worth doing anyway as they get you the snap gun.

Recent findings suggest that if you complete every job Yasmani has and keep asking for more, he'll also offer you a tip for $10,000 in Chapter 4. Pay it, and he'll give you the locations of two security vans (armored cars) in Vice City. They'll show up on your map as pink icons.

Towards the end of Chapter 4, after the main heist, if you haven't completed every job for Yasmani, you'll get the "That's Where the Money Is" opportunity to tail an armored car to a bank vault.

There are multiple banks with vaults that armored cars visit. While driving around the areas near these banks and keeping your eyes peeled, you may spot an armored car without Yasmani's tip. It could take quite a while, though!

Sources indicate that you can see which banks have vaults by looking under "Big Bank Jobs" in the "Robberies" category on your map. There are four big banks in Ocean Beach, two downtown, one in Tequesta, and one at Vice City International Airport.

Follow the armored car until it parks outside a bank, though make sure to keep your distance as otherwise he won't park. Watch as one of the drivers gets out and walks into the bank. You can follow him to see where he goes, though bank layouts differ and he may take different routes. He may walk through the front doors, or he may go in a side entrance or a roll-up door in the back.

Once he's all the way inside—not just inside the front doors, but deep into the bank—he'll head to the vault and open it.

According to recent reports, you can't open that vault yourself! Only the armored car driver can. That's the trick.

According to recent reports, once the guard is in the back of the bank, begin the robbery. Search for the vault in the back. You may need to use explosives to open the door the guard went through, or you can look for a door you can open with the snap gun. You'll find the vault door open with the armored car driver nearby. Subdue him and grab all the cash off the cart inside the vault.

According to recent reports, there are several safe deposit boxes in the vault you can open for extra loot. Use your focus ability to highlight which boxes you can loot, and shoot them to open them up. You can also blow open all the boxes at once using a grenade or sticky bomb. Grab the loot from each.

If you really want to clean the place out, there's still all the cash drawers in the front of the bank and a small safe, or multiple safes, somewhere else, usually in an office in the back. You can open these standard safes with safe codes.

It has been revealed that the armored car parked outside has loot in it, too. The thing is, it may despawn while you're inside the bank. If you want to loot it, place a sticky explosive on the rear door, which won't let the truck despawn. (Be stealthy: there's another guard still watching the truck). When you leave the bank after the robbery, detonate the bomb and grab the loot.

According to recent reports, the best way to enter a bank is through a back door, if the building has one, (using the snap gun to avoid alarms) or a roll-up door. If the guard you're following goes in the back, he may leave the doors unlocked behind him, and you may not even have to unlock any doors at all to reach the vault. Just be prepared to run into multiple security guards and employees you'll need to subdue.

You will want both Jason and Lucia along for any bank vault jobs you pull. There is so much cash and valuables to grab you'll easily fill up four bags, which requires two people to carry. (You can hand loot bags to your partner by interacting with them and choosing the "Hand over bag" prompt). You'll also want one character to work as crowd control while you're looting the bank.

A silenced gun is a good idea: you want to delay setting off alarms for as long as possible, and if bank employees or citizens hear gunshots they may panic and trigger the alarm, or flee from the bank and call the cops.

In a lot of robberies you can find the security footage and destroy it while the robbery is in progress. Big banks have cloud-based cameras which won't allow you to destroy the footage. Keep a lookout (using focus) for cameras and shoot them out (with silenced pistols) as rapidly as you can.

Sources indicate that if an alarm goes off during a vault robbery, you'll get an instant four-star wanted level, which means SWAT trucks, roadblocks, and helicopters. Park your car in a good spot outside so you can jump into it easily, and have some idea of where you want to drive to during your escape.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October.
  • That's according to market analysis firm Circana's latest US market report, which revealed Modern Warfare 4 was October's leader in dollar sales.
  • However, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October. The Infinity Ward-developed shooter was October's best-selling game in the US across digital and retail, beating the month's other major-hitters, including Gears of War: E-Day and Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

That's according to market analysis firm Circana's latest US market report, which revealed Modern Warfare 4 was October's leader in dollar sales. This marks the 19th-year running that a Call of Duty game topped the charts in its release month, a streak that began with November 2008's COD: World at War.

However, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers. In fact, the only COD title on the list is the Black Ops 2 port released this summer. NBA 2K27 continues to lead Circana's ranking, having overtaken Resident Evil: Requiem last month to secure the top spot. It's a reverse of Circana's September report, when NBA 2K27 failed to lead its own debut month but claimed the top spot in the year-to-date list. Here's the list of the top 10 year-to-date:.

Away from Modern Warfare 4, October saw the release of several other well-performing and critically acclaimed games, and six of the top ten were upcoming releases. That hasn't stopped Circana from posting 14 percent lower spending on games compared to October last year. Analyst Mat Piscatella noted much of that dip can be attributed to a massive slump in mobile spending, and also because October 2025 was particularly strong, with both Battlefield 6 and Pokémon Legends: Z-A releasing. Here's October's top 10:.

In Eurogamer's Modern Warfare 4 review, Dom Peppiatt awarded it four stars, writing: "Modern Warfare 4 represents the highest tide for Call of Duty in seven years. Infinity Ward needed to pull off a balancing act I don't envy; injecting just enough nostalgia into a series propped up with so many conventions and expectations there's barely room for anything latest, alongside enough innovation and intrigue to keep people interested.".

Breaking: "Game feel is impossible to copy": CEO of Probably Stolen publisher tinyBuild states devs "shouldn't be afraid" of AI clones

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GenAI game clones are apparently becoming a real enough threat to the industry that Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick pre-warned "this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent," while threatening legal action against anyone who naughtily tinkered with GTA VI.
  • Nichiporchik discusses tinyBuild's approach to the gap between announcement and release being notable in the age of slop copies (I am trying not to write 'sloppies' into my article, but it is tempting), explaining that "The traditional wisdom previously was to announce early, build up as many wishlists as possible over time, and then you'll have a good basis to launch your game eventually.
  • He recalls an example of someone making an Android port of Graveyard Keeper, which "barely fit into memory", and was surprised by how "easy" it seemed.

GenAI game clones are apparently becoming a real enough threat to the industry that Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick pre-warned "this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent," while threatening legal action against anyone who naughtily tinkered with GTA VI. More recently, one or more apparent crypto grifters claim to have naughtily tinkered with GTA VI, sparking attempts to vibe-recomp an unoffical PC version. However, contrasting Zelnick's position is tinyBuild CEO Alex Nichiporchik, who quite confidently stated in an interview with Gamesindustry.biz that "devs shouldn't be afraid of it.".

Nichiporchik discusses tinyBuild's approach to the gap between announcement and release being notable in the age of slop copies (I am trying not to write 'sloppies' into my article, but it is tempting), explaining that "The traditional wisdom previously was to announce early, build up as many wishlists as possible over time, and then you'll have a good basis to launch your game eventually. And that seems to be changing fundamentally." He adds that maintaining a short gap also helps as, to put it simply, "people have short memories, right?" And, unfortunately, he's right; there are so many games coming out that adding something to your wishlist often feels like resigning it to remembering it exists six months later.

He recalls an example of someone making an Android port of Graveyard Keeper, which "barely fit into memory", and was surprised by how "easy" it seemed. But then, he clarifies that the reason it seemed so easy was a lack of care. "There's a reason that every kind of AI slop game feels the same; it's because when you try to make something from zero, AI will multiply your skills, and zero times a thousand is still zero." The people claiming to 'develop' recomps do not care for making a game that feels right, or even one that works; they care only for the short-lived dopamine of being popular on Twitter for fifteen minutes before another slop copy rears its head (and is inevitably revealed to be jankware). Nichiporchik specifies that "game feel is impossible to copy; as long as you have a great game feel and a great game loop, I think you're going to be okay." 'Game feel' is one of the vaguest terms that exists in this field, but I do feel that it refers to something tangible and immediately noticeable when it's gone.

It has been revealed that for example, I've recently been replaying the wonderful Celeste, and the 'game feel' of its wavedashing is core to making the practice of blazing through levels so engaging. The wavedash works the same every time, due to precise programming from Extremely OK Games spending time and effort painstakingly ensuring it did in the interest of consistency and unity in movement mechanics. You can't make good art without caring about the quality, even if there are now faster ways to knock together a 'working' game. To borrow an overused but still salient phrase: AI could never.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse has today delivered full details on the next major upgrade for Honkai: Star Rail. Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a new chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The new narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

The Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

Sources indicate that while the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

Recent findings suggest that the benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Sources indicate that version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a new Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

Sources indicate that you can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can initiative where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another fresh addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

According to recent reports, there’s more coming down the line, too. A new Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

  • Industry observers note that the case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Closing statements in Rockstar and IWGB's employment tribunal case - revolving around the GTA 6 developer's alleged 'union busting' and the firing of 34 employees - have now been read, bringing the hearing to an end. There's currently no timeline for a verdict, however, with one commentator suggesting a judgement could take weeks or months to arrive.

Industry observers note that the case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights. Rockstar has been accused of unlawfully firing workers for being part of a union, but the GTA developer insists employees were dismissed for breaching confidentiality agreements.

People Makes Games' Chris Bratt has been following the case closely and reporting on proceedings as they've unfolded. With closing statements now complete, Bratt quoted Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying, "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as promptly as I possibly can.".

According to recent reports, however, Bratt suggests it could be ""anywhere from a few weeks up to a few months before we actually hear the judgement", noting "The firings themselves, let's not forget, happened over a year ago now. This has been a slog.".

It has been revealed that one fired Rockstar worker involved in the case spoke with Bratt after the closing statements to share their thoughts. "Honestly it's just sort of blended together," they said. "It’s been so long, that after the first six months or so it became the new depressing reality. I'm hoping the judgement will release us from it.".

Last month, the conclusion of the tribunal hearing was delayed after cross examination of witnesses ran long.

Yesterday's closing statements come at a time when all eyes are on GTA 6 as it finally releases this week, concluding years of development for both current and former employees. Many of those workers involved in the case urged players to support the game despite the legal dispute.

In a recent development, additionally, Rockstar employees are at the moment voting on whether they want recognised union representation at the studio. If the vote passes, it would be the largest recognised union across the entirety of the UK video game industry. The deadline for union votes is 26th November.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, there was a 93.2% turnout in the ballot, which commenced in early November, with 1,163 Rockstar employees voting against the deal and 381 voting in favor.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Now that GTA 6 is finally here after 13 long years, a good chunk of attention has shifted to developer Rockstar and its workers' recent vote against a union recognition deal – a vote that arguably came as a surprise to many on the outside.

In a recent development, there was a 93.2% turnout in the ballot, which commenced in early November, with 1,163 Rockstar employees voting against the deal and 381 voting in favor. These figures add up to a split of 75.3% and 24.7% – numbers that some devs feel make sense. Associate principal vehicle AI programmer Thomas March, for example, is one such dev, taking to LinkedIn to share why he was part of the majority vote himself.

It has been revealed that "Today, my coworkers and I voted against union recognition at Rockstar North," he writes. "These of course are just my own personal views, but I wanted to add some context for why I did this. The gaming industry has been a terrible and terrifying industry over the past few years, and I can understand why so many people would find this decision confusing." He's not wrong, judging by reactions to the vote – but he feels Rockstar is different.

It has been revealed that "Rockstar has always been a place that enormously values and rewards individual creativity, and putting a union between the close friendships and relationships with the people that made this all possible was not the right decision," March continues. "It was endlessly frustrating to hear the IWGB [Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain] claim I was being exploited, to see them celebrate the delay of our game and to ridicule the people who make everything I do possible.".

Recent findings suggest that the dev then explains why he disagrees with the IWGB – which dubbed Rockstar's firing of over 30 employees last year "ruthless" and has repeatedly spoken out against the company's practices."I've been more taken care of at Rockstar than any place I've ever worked," he states. "Nowhere else have I been listened to so closely, treated with such respect, even while working with veterans and experts bar none.".

It has been revealed that march doesn't end his praise there, saying he "never" had any of his calls "overruled," or any concerns ignored. "I was given absolute freedom and trust to make my contributions to the game the best they could be. And on top of that, the benefits of working here, the healthcare, the allowances, the food and drink and snacks, it has always been astonishing beyond description to see an employer genuinely care for our wellbeing," he goes on.

"I never worked a minute of overtime that wasn't purely my own decision and driven by my own passion, and every minute was paid back to me with interest. And no matter what time I left the office, I would see our management all the way to the top leaving later still... and yet they'd thank me for my contributions." With all of this in mind, March notes he's saddened to see all of the outrage surrounding Rockstar.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

"It breaks my heart to hear people saying that they don't want to work here, citing headlines that claim crunch, bad working conditions, and exploitation," he concludes. "Rockstar is, by far, the best place I've ever worked. It is not a cautionary tale, it is an exemplary example – not just in making the most incredible and generational games of all time, but also as a workplace." Obviously, though, this is one voice of many.

Former devs have shared different views in the past, with some instructing fans to not boycott GTA 6 but rather "support our legal battle instead" and "win justice for the people who helped make" the game but faced dismissal before it could release. Animation programmer Nestor Uriarte also noted he's "worried about getting laid off" even after "working on the biggest game of all time" – you know, Grand Theft Auto 6.

Others outside of the studio have also expressed fears over more layoffs now that the newly introduced Grand Theft Auto is here. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen is one such dev. She hoped that the GTA 6 devs would be "successful in unionizing." Finance experts like Square Enix veteran Jacob Novak also stated the game's success indeed isn't enough to stop layoffs.

Industry observers note that that's all just to say that March's stance – while completely valid – isn't the only one out there. That's the whole point of a vote, I suppose, and his take (while not the sole POV out there) provides a bit of insight perhaps on why it swayed the way it did.

Have a look at our GTA 6 review to learn how we feel about one of the biggest new games this year, or check our GTA 6 guide for more about Rockstar's behemoth release.

US President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he'd given Nvidia "assurance" that ousted and now reinstated CEO Jensen Huang did not represent a national security threat despite an affair with a woman who was reportedly in contact with China's top spy agency.

Trump provided that assurance without any formal investigation into Huang's dealings.

Sources indicate that on whether Huang had been investigated, US Attorney General Todd Blanche noted during a press conference this week, "I don't want to talk about investigation. What does that mean, had Huang been investigated? For what? I don't understand the question.".

Blanche also stated that he did not know about any export control investigation related to Nvidia, even though potential violations of export control law are the central concern of the scandal.

"A critical national security threat in the Nvidia situation is that Jensen Huang shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law, in what amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race," Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer remarked on Tuesday.

According to recent reports, according to sources speaking to Reuters, Trump's assurance to the Nvidia board was based on investigations into Nvidia clients Super Micro Computer and Megaspeed International, the latter of which is the manufacturer associated with Alice Huang (no relation), the woman with whom Huang admitted to having an affair. (The CEO also reportedly had affairs with Nvidia employees.).

Recent findings suggest that in his return address to Nvidia staff, Huang said (via Marisa Kabas) that the manufacturer's board opted to bring him back of their own accord, not because of pressure from the Trump administration. That statement is contradicted by Trump himself, who told CNBC that he "convinced" the Nvidia board to bring Huang back.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As GTA 6 finally arrives, increasingly outspoken games industry legend Warren Spector - known for seminal immersive sims including Deus Ex - has offered both praise for the game's achievements and lambasted its "billion dollar" development model, writing, "I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it’s the best we have to offer".

In a recent development, spector declared his retirement from games development in August following struggles at his OtherSide Entertainment studio, and has been vocal about the state of the games industry in the months since, notably saying anyone at EA responsible for the "travesty" of BioWare's closure should be "ashamed". And now Spector has taken on GTA 6.

"First, congratulations to everyone who worked on GTA 6. It looks like it will be a high point of sorts for our medium and our business," he wrote in a post on LinkedIn. "However… its billion dollar development cost and an undoubtedly crazy marketing budget don't represent a business model anyone else can or probably should emulate.

Sources indicate that "That's especially true," Spector continued, "when thousands of developers are out of work. A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries. Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is.".

According to recent reports, the "sure success" of GTA 6 proves a point he's made "for years", he said: "That no game that matters ships on time and/or on budget". Highlighting GTA 6's year-long delay and reported billion dollar budget, Spector suggested, "Give a game the time and money to prove its potential (key word, potential) and you have a chance of making something great. Underfund a game or force it out the door before it's ready [is] guaranteed failure no matter how much potential it has.

"So, again, congratulations," Spector concluded. "Ambition and innovation are necessary for the medium to reach its potential. I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it's the best we have to offer.".

Industry observers note that despite Spector's concerns, GTA 6's arrival is, as expected, already causing shockwaves across the industry. It has broken pre-order records for Xbox and PlayStation stores, smashed the all-time livestream viewer record, and apparently briefly broke Reddit too. And is its success deserved? Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell thinks so, saying it "pushes back the horizon of video games once again" in his five star GTA 6 review.

In a recent development, the developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:.

It has been revealed that episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a new Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

Breaking: Does GTA 6 have an 'easy mode'? Not officially, but there are two very important settings you can change to make the game less difficult

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that by now, you've probably heard that you cannot use cheats in GTA 6 until you complete the main story.
  • But, for anyone looking to have a slightly easier time with GTA 6 than the dev's intended experience, I come with good news: you can make the game a little bit easier by toggling two options in the game's Settings menu.
  • According to recent reports, 'Accessible Combat' decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that by now, you've probably heard that you cannot use cheats in GTA 6 until you complete the main story. Not only that, but enabling cheat codes also locks story progression and deactivates the ability to save. Basically, you can use cheats to have a quick crime spree and blow off some steam, then it's back to normalcy. Understandably, some gamers are a little put out with this change.

But, for anyone looking to have a slightly easier time with GTA 6 than the dev's intended experience, I come with good news: you can make the game a little bit easier by toggling two options in the game's Settings menu. If you open Settings, and then navigate to Gameplay, you'll find 'Accessible Combat' and 'Reduced Vehicle Damage' toggles. You can activate both to make GTA 6's more difficult elements a little bit easier to work through.

According to recent reports, 'Accessible Combat' decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider. 'Reduced Vehicle Damage', as you'd expect, lowers the damage taken by your vehicle and allows your ride to endure more punishment. This applies to gunfire, environmental threats, and impact damage.

Industry observers note that toggle these settings comes with a warning from Rockstar, though. A prompt notes that enabling these modifiers will "significantly change the balance and experience of the gameplay". I've been playing around with these settings and whilst they are not a foolproof 'God Mode' by any means, you can absolutely see a difference in the game when they're enabled: Jason and Lucia take a lot more punishment from melee damage and gunshots, and I had to really try to get Jason's old banged up pickup into even the 'slightly smoking' bracket of disrepair. Your mileage may vary, but these settings, from what I can tell so far, certainly do make the game easier.

Given that cheats disable trophies and progression, these settings might be something to keep in mind if you're trying to find a smoother path through the main story of GTA 6. It's a credit to Rockstar's accessibility teams that these have been included at all - alongside the 23 other gameplay accessibility options, the 12 display options, the 70 UI options, the 24 camera options, and the 14 audio options.

Recent findings suggest that "We create inclusive, intuitive, and immersive experiences for every player," noted Rockstar's associate UI director, Sam Grosset, in materials provided to Eurogamer ahead of the game's launch. "Accessibility is considered from the outset, and designing for diverse needs enables us to create better games for everyone. We wanted every player in GTA 6 to have options to play the game how they like. Whether it's selecting a larger font size, opting for a more minimal screen experience, or making a controls tweak to sprinting... the choices are open to all.".

We also learned yesterday that Rockstar has made GTA 6 missions "harder to fail" by making them more open-ended, and giving players more ways to figure out how to do things in their own way.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Every now and again, we hear grumbles from some parts of the Xbox community that they're frustrated when games are unveiled and Xbox doesn't make a big deal about how those titles are specifically first-party creations.

In other words, some fans want Xbox to shout from the rooftops about its own games for its own platform, and not to make them immediately look like third-party titles. There's been some discussion about this on social media this week with Xbox megafan Klobrille and Windows Central editor Jez Corden, highlighting situations like StarCraft, Diablo V and new Fallout games where it felt like they were announced without any real references to Xbox.

And, when Corden stated that "Xbox is really weak at linking its games to its brand", it prompted Xbox CSO Matthew Ball to get involved in the discussion and promise that the situation is being fixed in 2027.

Who knows what "fixed" means in this regard, but it sounds like the team at Xbox is going to be more proactive at promoting the brand when an Xbox Game Studios, Activision Blizzard or Bethesda title is announced / shown off.

That doesn't necessarily mean anything in terms of exclusives and multi-platform titles (we assume we'll still get some of the latter), but hopefully it'll be much clearer to the average consumer when a game is an in-house Xbox game.

In a recent development, let's see what happens in the New Year, eh? We've got Fable just around the corner in a couple of months' time, and then the likes of Clockwork: Revolution and Spyro: A Realm Reborn (which is only published by Xbox, but nevertheless still counts!) along with whatever else Xbox might have in store for us in 2027.

Breaking: "It would end up appealing to no one": The Witcher 4 narrative leads aren't willing to strip away the series' "distinct edge" in the name of chasing a broader audience

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (599 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent interview with Korean outlet Inven, CD Projekt Red's narrative director Philipp Weber and vice president of story Marcin Blacha shared some words on The Witcher 4, focusing on their awareness that not only will it inevitably be different from The Witcher 3, but also that it needs to be in order to justify its existence.
  • Weber describes the core of a 'Witcher-like' story to be something that "explores the various facets of human nature — a game for adults", which he clarifies doesn't just mean violence or sex, but "treating the player as a mature adult, asking difficult questions without offering easy answers." While it has been quite a while since its predecessor, they still feel that the upcoming sequel must be true to the series it's part of and earn that numbered title: "If we were to strip away The Witcher's distinct edge just to reach a broader audience, it would end up appealing to no one.".
  • Industry observers note that of course, the biggest change is that of the protagonist, from Geralt to Ciri.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent interview with Korean outlet Inven, CD Projekt Red's narrative director Philipp Weber and vice president of story Marcin Blacha shared some words on The Witcher 4, focusing on their awareness that not only will it inevitably be different from The Witcher 3, but also that it needs to be in order to justify its existence. Simultaneously, there's a certain something to The Witcher as a series that they feel is difficult to make tangible, but is something they want to ensure they don't lose sight of.

Weber describes the core of a 'Witcher-like' story to be something that "explores the various facets of human nature — a game for adults", which he clarifies doesn't just mean violence or sex, but "treating the player as a mature adult, asking difficult questions without offering easy answers." While it has been quite a while since its predecessor, they still feel that the upcoming sequel must be true to the series it's part of and earn that numbered title: "If we were to strip away The Witcher's distinct edge just to reach a broader audience, it would end up appealing to no one.".

Industry observers note that of course, the biggest change is that of the protagonist, from Geralt to Ciri. Blacha explains that "Ciri isn't calm and composed like Geralt, nor does she hide her emotions easily. She is far more hot-headed and tends to be emotional when making decisions." In terms of how this actually affects the narrative itself and the protagonist's place in it, he elaborates that "when playing as Geralt, players acted more like an arbiter judging how to resolve a situation. When playing as Ciri, you are much more deeply involved in the story through her personal perspective." It's an interesting notion, to state that the difference in role is that where Geralt was more of a fixer, Ciri actually approaches situations on an interpersonal level. Weber seemingly half-jokes that "we find ourselves in a position very similar to Ciri's. Just as Ciri must succeed Geralt, we must create a game that lives up to The Witcher 3.".

As for how The Witcher 4 will play, moment to moment, Weber explains that some inspiration has been taken from Cyberpunk 2077 in regards to its open, player-led approach to customisation and, as a result, quests. "You could be a netrunner or a cyber ninja air-dashing into a scene with a double jump. We had to account for all those possibilities available to the player," he recalls. While I can't imagine Ciri will be air-dashing around Kovir, this statement does make me wonder how this approach can be applied to a game with such a specific existing protagonist, rather than the blank slate of Cyberpunk 2077's V. Recalling the side content of The Witcher 3 and its acclaim, he believes that people loved them "because we strived to offer something fresh" and "didn't create quests that merely waste the player's time", which is a principle that "remains unchanged today." Later, he condenses his feelings into the mantra that "A great quest can stem from a compelling story, an engaging character, or fantastic gameplay alone, but overall, there must be harmony.".

Towards the end of the interview, Blacha jokes that "One of our greatest achievements is convincing people to finish their workday, buy our game, and then clock into another job as a character inside the game." It's quite a long and engaging read, so if you're invested in The Witcher IV and its narrative development, I do encourage you read the entire thing.

The Grand Final of the tournament will take place on November 29th at 11am UTC+0 through to 4pm UTC+0 after three days of global competitive action.

Industry observers note that it’s the first Chinese esports title to reach DreamHack, featuring teams that have been selected through a full professional league system. Six regions offered a route to the offline finals, and the twelve squads competing this weekend are as follows:.

Fnatic are, of course, well known to DreamHack audiences, having won the first League of Legends World Championship there back in 2011, as well as the first CS:GO Major in 2013. Alliance, being a Swedish team, will be playing on home soil, but only time will tell if this gives them an additional boost. They, and the ten other teams to have gone the distance, will once again be competing for a share of a $500,000 prize pool.

One core aspect of Delta Force that’s attracted upcoming fans over the last twelve months is its commitment to extraction as an esport. Whereas in traditional FPS competitions there’s an obvious focus on winning fights, in Delta Force’s Operations mode, information gathering, firefights, resource management and extraction decisions all play out within a single match.

It has been revealed that UPDATE 5PM GMT: Actors Manni L. Perez and Dylan Rourke have announced their involvement in GTA 6, in portraying Lucia and Jason, respectively, in the game.

In a recent development, dylan Rourke wrote on Instagram: "Years witnessing the hardest working and most skilled artisans game making has to offer. A photo accompanying the post demonstrates the actors posing in front of a billboard advertising the game.

A post shared by Dylan Rourke (@dylan_rourke).

ORIGINAL STORY 3PM GMT: Rockstar has finally declared the full cast list for Grand Theft Auto 6, having left fans speculating right up to the game's release about which actors play the game's leads.

Recent findings suggest that lucia's actor Manni L. Perez was revealed through her nomination for The Game Awards, and it nearly took a photo taken by Lucia's stunt double Victoria Lee to reveal who played Jason.

"After keeping my mouth shut for YEEAARRSSS (and what feels like FOREVER!!!), I can finally share that I've been lucky enough to help bring Lucia to life as her main stunt double in Grand Theft Auto 6, along with a whole bunch of other characters stunts along the way!" Lee wrote in a picture of her and Manni, and rumoured Jason actor Dylan Rourke, on Instagram.

Sources indicate that "A special shoutout to Manni and Dylan! You two are truly amazing humans, inside and out! So much talent, heart, and genuine goodness. I'm forever grateful to have shared this wild ride with you both!" she added.

And Rockstar's official cast list for GTA 6 confirms that yes, it is Dylan Rourke who plays the role.

A post shared by Victoria Lee (@victoria_lee_stunts).

Rourke's own Instagram account doesn't feature any news of his involvement in GTA 6, but his name was referenced in a recent IGN Holland article, as spotted on Reddit, earlier today.

Stephen Root, who plays Brian Heder, was the only actor to confirm his involvement in GTA 6 prior to the game's release, though it's a name many people had already guessed following the game's Netflix extended look.

Capcom's quirky dinosaur-fighting hero shooter is shutting down in 2027

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that "Exoprimal is a throwback to weird, experimental early 2000s Capcom," we wrote of the team-based hero shooter ahead of its launch back in 2023.
  • Industry observers note that despite that intriguing premise, the end result was not particularly memorable: Perfectly fine, and with some fantastic ideas, but "more like an early access phase than a finished game," we wrote in our 69% review.
  • In a recent development, but now that's changing too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that "Exoprimal is a throwback to weird, experimental early 2000s Capcom," we wrote of the team-based hero shooter ahead of its launch back in 2023. While ostensibly about battling dinosaurs, "you first go through an interdimensional time portal controlled by a rogue AI, and then you compete in a Hunger Games-style contest against alternate universe versions of yourself for the AI's amusement. That's where the dinosaur killing comes in.".

Industry observers note that despite that intriguing premise, the end result was not particularly memorable: Perfectly fine, and with some fantastic ideas, but "more like an early access phase than a finished game," we wrote in our 69% review. And it didn't catch on: A year later, Capcom announced the end of upcoming updates for the game, although the game remained fully playable.

In a recent development, but now that's changing too. Capcom declared today that Exoprimal services will be terminated on September 29, 2027, at which point the game will become unplayable. "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years," Capcom wrote, "and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement.".

It has been revealed that the sale of seasonal "survival passes," which have been rotating through Exoprimal's four seasons since the end of updates in 2024, has been halted, while the game itself along with all DLC and "other products"—there's quite a lot of it—will be removed from sale on March 30, 2027. After that, the game will tick on—and Capcom hopes you will continue to enjoy it—until the end of the road in September.

Recent findings suggest that it sucks to see games fail, especially when they have the potential to grow into something good, and it's even worse when they don't just tank but become completely unplayable because of their reliance on external servers that no longer exist. This is one of the primary drivers behind efforts like Stop Killing Games: Wherever possible, the end of a game's service should not signal the end of the game.

According to recent reports, it's a principle I broadly support, but in the case of Exoprimal it's fair to say that not too many people will be impacted by the shutdown: SteamDB indicates that the peak concurrent player count over the past 24 hours was just 23. Exoprimal is also available on consoles so there are more players in total than just that, but how many more? I don't know, but I'd guess not too many.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following a round of layoffs last month that resulted in the loss of 40 jobs, which itself came after a previous source of funding pulled out in the Spring, independent studio Gravity Well has now revealed that it is going into "hibernation" for the foreseeable future. The team was largely made up of devs who'd left Titanfall and Apex Legends studio Respawn Entertainment, and under the Gravity Well banner had been working on a upcoming, still-unannounced game for around six years.

A statement posted to the main page on Gravity Well's site reads:.

"We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building. Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we’re going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you’re a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation.

If you’re a publisher or investor and are interested in talking, let's connect!".

The message is signed off by its founders Drew McCoy, Jon 'Slothy' Shiring and Mon Saetern. Besides being the second project led by former Respawn developers to be doomed this year - see also Wildlight's Highguard - it's unfortunately another case of a studio made up of developers with incredible pedigrees being left at the whim of funding accruement in the current state of the industry. That said, it is noteworthy that the team have not shown anything publicly in the six years since their formation, minus a few pieces of concept art which can now be seen on its site. It's still unknown exactly what Gravity Well was working on, but it's likely to have been some kind of movement-based shooter, if the teams' experience on Titanfall, Apex Legends and Call of Duty is anything to go by. Solidarity to all affected, who I hope can find work elsewhere in the industry.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We already knew there'd be a frantic clamour for GTA 6 this week, and we also knew plenty of players would be eyeing up Xbox's 'New Zealand trick' to get in on the action early. But it's now being reported that a whopping 2m UK and US players took advantage of the trick - which, for context, equals more than a third of New Zealand's actual population.

Here's a quick bit of background: Rockstar's regional release schedule meant GTA 6 launched at midnight on 19th November everywhere, local time. As such, Newly introduced Zealand was the first country in the world to see the hugely anticipated game go live, thanks to timezones. And because Xbox players can make purchases on any regional store easily, simply by changing their console's country, understandably impatient sorts opted to become temporary virtual New Zealand residents in their droves (on PlayStation, the process requires a regional account and payment in local currency so is more finicky).

Recent findings suggest that in fact, according to data analytics firm Ampere Analysis, the early demand was such that 1.5m Xbox people in the US and 600,000 UK Xbox players briefly went Kiwi for the occasion of GTA 6's launch. Other countries highlighted by Ampere include Canada, where 200,000 Xbox players took the New Zealand plunge, Brazil (200,000 players), and Mexico (100,000 players).

By contrast, just 100,000 PlayStation players in the US opted to dive in early, reflecting, as Ampere notes, "the ease of being able to switch country in the account settings on Xbox consoles." And here's all that info in graph form:.

Sources indicate that amusingly, Newly introduced Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Some hours later and the rest of the world can now finally, officially join in the GTA 6 fun, and it's a game worth playing. Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell called it an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in his five star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The smartypants over at Digital Foundry are still putting in the work, this time going deep into the nitty gritty of how well GTA 6 performs when streamed through the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One.
  • Following their rigorous testing on Xbox Series X and Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro, the boffin boys have now spent a good week putting streamed performance, latency and image quality under the cosh.
  • Xbox Cloud Gaming is streamed from Microsoft servers which means the version of GTA 6 you'll be playing is the Xbox Series S version.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The smartypants over at Digital Foundry are still putting in the work, this time going deep into the nitty gritty of how well GTA 6 performs when streamed through the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One.

Following their rigorous testing on Xbox Series X and Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro, the boffin boys have now spent a good week putting streamed performance, latency and image quality under the cosh.

Xbox Cloud Gaming is streamed from Microsoft servers which means the version of GTA 6 you'll be playing is the Xbox Series S version. Of course, this means the drawbacks present on the Series S version are also present in the Xbox Cloud streamed one.

According to recent reports, "Let's start with nuts and bolts of the experience. As with other Xbox Cloud Gaming titles, which are streamed from Microsoft servers rather than your own console, the version of GTA 6 you're getting here is the Xbox Series S version. That means a few things just by the nature of the Series S port itself - slightly ropey performance, quality setting cutbacks across the board and a 720p base image upscaled to 1080p using FSR 4.1. However, you do at least get all of the game's major effects intact, including ray-traced lighting, ray-traced reflections and strand-based hair.".

Performance begins where you'd expect on Xbox Series S, clocking around 20-30FPS. However, Digital Foundry notes that "frame pacing is significantly worse than the real deal, with quicker 16.7ms frames and slower 50.0ms frames surrounding the expected 33.3ms ones.".

Industry observers note that from their Xbox One Cloud tests, they used an ethernet connection, and were genuinely impressed with GTA 6's image quality. They mentioned the game isn't "significantly degraded by the streaming process", with little visible compression or artefacting when in motion. Stood still, it's hardly noticeable too.

It has been revealed that streaming GTA 6 at 1440p (via Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on One S or X) also appears to benefit from a higher bitrate than usual, with DF stating it gets a "higher bitrate than that afforded to other games". For context, GTA 6 streamed at about 37mbps, compared to the recently released Control: Resonant, which only got 15-27mbps.

Latency also looks to be the major winner in testing. Digital Foundry tested GTA 6 running natively on Xbox Series S with the streamed version on Xbox One, finding the latter only added a mere 9ms to latency. Barely noticeable.

Recent findings suggest that "Latency is also exceptional - at least in context. We measured around an extra 9ms of added latency compared to running GTA 6 locally on Series S - 184.5ms vs 175.2ms -which is essentially imperceptible for a game that is running on all consoles with around 160 to 180ms of latency anyway. That makes the pace relatively sedate, even when driving or shooting, but it's something that you can get used to over time, and the cloud version doesn't change the equation here. These numbers come from a console attached via ethernet cable to a high-speed fibre connection with a wired controller; your mileage may vary based on location, internet speed, controller latency, display latency and so on.".

So, GTA 6 looks decent and feels comparably responsive controller in hand, with the biggest drawback to streaming the game on Xbox One being that it pulls from an Xbox Series S version, and not the Series X version of the game.

In a recent development, of course, if you can't access current-gen hardware, Digital Foundry thinks streaming GTA 6 through the Xbox Cloud app on Xbox One is a pretty good way to experience the universally acclaimed RPG. But that generally comes with Cloud Playtime charges, including if you go beyond your monthly allotted hours on Xbox Game Pass.

Have you tried Xbox Cloud streaming GTA VI? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

According to recent reports, TV hours in general are known for being grueling, and late night is its own beast when it comes to hours worked. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Phantom Blade Zero studio S-Game has announced the game's next PS5 patch will arrive this Saturday, 28th November 2026, weighing in at around 7GB.

It's already posted the patch notes ahead of pushing the PS5 revision live at the weekend, and they reveal new features, technical enhancements, and bug fixes coming to the game.

The most substantial additions are two fresh features: a Combat Assist section in the settings and an Automatic Strong Camera Assist setting.

"With this option turned off, strong camera assistance applies only while you are attacking an enemy. At other times, the camera makes only minor adjustments.".

It has been revealed that on the technical front, the amount of video memory and system memory the title uses has been reduced, which should improve the performance of cutscenes and general gameplay in snow-covered areas. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously confirmed operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry.
  • GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.
  • The publication also understands the cuts, stated to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture revealed last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously confirmed operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. It indicates the cuts are necessary "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.".

GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.

The publication also understands the cuts, stated to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture revealed last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.

In a statement provided to Eurogamer, Ubisoft confirmed it is, "reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations", adding: "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

Sources indicate that "We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues," the statement continued. "We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

Recent findings suggest that these latest job cuts are part of a "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" revealed by Ubisoft in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Recent findings suggest that since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Traditionally, Black Friday deals have been focused on spending money, but a special subcategory of deals actually lets you buy money. That's because over at Amazon, quite a few gift cards are reduced, letting you spend less money on a card than their financial value actually is.

There are plenty of gift card deals at Amazon, and that includes a few reductions which will be particularly interesting for gamers. The actual selection of gaming gift card deals is limited (to, uh, one), but there are also movie theater chains and fast food outlets which have their gift cards reduced too. So we'll hopefully be able to find you something useful to you, or that you'd happily give to someone.

The 15% reduced from the cost of this Domino's gift card only applies to the $50 option, but that's all you'll need for a family meal or indulgent movie night.

Sources indicate that this discount only applies to $50 gift cards and, strangely, only certain designs. Oh well; the look of the gift card doesn't matter if you're getting more for your money.

This Cinemark gift card doesn't just let you buy theater tickets for less, but it also applies to the chain's cafes and restaurants too.

A 20% discount in the price of a gift card to Regal theaters means you can visit the major theater group for a lower price, and you're going to get plenty of snacks for the reduced price.

Know a Roblox fan? This gift card is 15% reduced, saving a bit of money to spend on Robux. The card also lets them get some extra perks across the game when it's redeemed.

This Taco Bell eGift card deal is a bit different: you need to redeem it when ordering from the app, not in person. The 15% discount only applies to the $50 card, not any of the other ones offered.

Industry observers note that for an alternative fast-food chain which has discounted gift cards, Panera Bread's $50 physical gift card is 20% off. However the $25 or $75 alternatives aren't reduced at all.

Sources indicate that on the surface, a reduction in a gift card seems like a nice little way to save money on a gift, or a workaround to get a cheaper meal or theater ticket. But they're a little better than you'd first think.

Recent findings suggest that usually, when a retailer or outlet is offering promotions, it'll let you pick a certain one. You generally can't double promotions in most shops, so you have to pick whichever is best for your purchase.

Sources indicate that however if you're paying for said purchase with a reduced gift card, that often doesn't count as a promotion. In short, if Domino's is running several deals on pizzas, you'd usually only need to pick one; if you're using a gift card you bought for less, this effectively acts as a second deal.

This is generally the case, but not always, and you can be sure by checking the small print in the Amazon listing before you buy it.

Industry observers note that just check before you buy the card: some of these are physical ones, which can only be used in the brand's branches, and others are online ones that can only be redeemed in certain places. Make sure you're buying a gift card that you, or your recipient, can actually use.

And before you start planning an elaborate system: you can't use a gift card to buy a gift card. That'd be an amazing hack that'd save you literally infinite money if done enough times, but the shops are way ahead of you and prohibit that.

We've found all of the Black Friday retro deals you might want to spend money on, and you can also find Black Friday toy deals to tempt you.

It has been revealed that another day, another Steam update! Earlier this year, Valve made some tweaks to Steam's Community Market as part of their ongoing widening of the digital storefront. The maybe Half-Life 3 developer is back with another update for the Community Market, once again bringing some fresh UI/UX bits, as well as some quality of life adjustments that should make it a bit nicer to use.

For starters, there's a new Market home page! "We've rebuilt the Market Home to load faster and present you with the most relevant items from your games," a blog post explains. "Instead of the Popular Items section, which was a small and static slice of millions of items, Trending Items will give you a glimpse into what’s new in the games you’re currently playing. The game links move up to the top spot and are now personalized, so rather than a flat and unchanging list, you get quick access to the items you're most likely to be interested in.".

Sources indicate that next up in the patch is the addition of a watchlist feature. Before, if you wanted to follow a number of items in the marketplace you'd need to bookmark everything, but now you can just save things to your watchlist; this includes the likes of specific listings, particular item types with any filters you've applied, and even specific searches, again with filters and search text. You can also apply custom names to watchlist entries in case two of them end up looking particularly similar.

There were a few other smaller bits to this enhancement too. You'll find a new section that highlights Steam community items, i.e. trading cards and emotes, from games you've played. If you have anything listed on the marketplace, you can now change the price without having to relist it. There's a list view option while browsing items. And market pages now load faster and are more responsive. A convenient sounding update for the Steam Community Market connoisseur! Which is already live, by the way.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.

The UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn. You'll need to have finished the game's first chapter, and it's most reliable after 2am in-game.

As word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it. Follow the trail into the trees towards a blue glow, and you'll catch a UFO beaming down on a woman before it drops her and flies off. Head back to her car, as she requests, and the UFO returns for you. You apparently black out and come round three days later, and a bronze trophy called The Truth Is Out There should unlock.

You can seemingly trigger the event as either Jason or Lucia, and it isn't needed for 100 percent completion.

And that's not the only close encounter you can expect, either. YouTuber Lazarbeam bumped into Bigfoot on the afternoon of 18th November, hours before the game rolled out in the UK, while one Reddit user reported that they weren't quite sure what they'd stumbled on, titling their post "I think I found Bigfoot".

Leonida's version of Bigfoot is actually the Skunk Ape, Florida's own swamp cryptid, and it can be found in the swamplands near Cottonmouth Lake in Mariana County as soon as free roam opens up. Listen out for a loud roar, then use Jason's tracking ability to follow it through the swamp. You may find it feeding on a deer carcass, while a second sighting has been reported south of Watson Bay.

In a recent development, either way, the trail seemingly ends at a strange, human-like tree. Investigate it, and Jason blacks out, triggering a short cutscene in which the creature creeps up on him, as shown in this video. He later wakes near his vehicle, drenched in sweat. Save your ammo, though, as shooting at it won't do you any good.

Cryptids and aliens are, of course, something of a Rockstar tradition by this point. GTA 5's Mount Chiliad mystery kept players hunting for years, and Output Lag has already spotted two NPCs in a GTA 6 bar talking about goings-on there. Nobody has cracked a full Chiliad-style puzzle in the new game yet, but I'm sure that's just a matter of when, not if.

GTA 6 debuted today on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, although some have been getting in on the action earlier as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even Newly introduced Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

It certainly seemed that way based on the reaction to Warhammer Survivors from Vampire Survivors veterans, who complained about its grindiness compared to their beloved bullet heaven originator, despite the arc of both games being quite similar. Developers Auroch Digital made Warhammer Survivors in partnership with Vampire Survivors creator Poncle, so of course the two games have a lot in common.

Other complaints were more valid. The Beasts of Nurgle did have too many hit points, and their ability to regenerate only exacerbated that. The treasure chest-opening animation did take a bit too long. And some of the weapons were undertuned. Fortunately, those complications and more have been addressed in hotfix v2.18. Here are the highlights:.

The change to XP is an interesting one. It's a standard part of the genre's formula to have random XP drops—killing some enemies gives you nothing, while others drop XP gems and tempt you to rush into a mob to grab them. Making every enemy drop at least a low-value XP gem will speed up leveling a bit, but hopefully when you see green or red gems you'll still want to risk a mob of orks to yoink.

Sources indicate that auroch Digital recently revealed a roadmap of upcoming additions to Warhammer Survivors, with the first substantial patch in December promising more characters, weapons, and weapon evolutions. January's updates will add more quality-of-life and balance improvements, as well as cross-save, with another update in the first quarter of 2027 bringing another round of characters, weapons, and weapon evolutions.

According to recent reports, the final item on the roadmap is a tease that simply states, "ERROR… Details classified." It's probably not the addition of a whole extra universe to its current Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar settings, but I'd be stoked to see them add the other popular world of Warhammer. By which I mean Blood Bowl, of course.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever now has more people playing each week than World of Warcraft has seen in 15 years, according to Blizzard.

"Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years!" executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale posted. "Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever!".

Longdale was quoting a post from the official World of Warcraft account, which shared a batch of "By the Numbers" stats for the newly introduced edition.

Since it rolled out on 4th November, players have created 15,160,147 characters and 140,764 guilds, completed 1,480,343,357 quests, and defeated 9,786,925,806 enemies.

In a recent development, another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years! Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever! 💙♾️ https://t.co/bMLQduLri2.

They've also formed 71,309,889 parties, used 28,696,386 camping items, and there have been 28,938,569 PvP kills.

Collectively, we've died a lot, too - 196,851,761 times in total, with Archmage Arugal, the final boss of Shadowfang Keep, seemingly the deadliest boss.

"You're breaking records by the day!" the post read.

Earlier this month, Blizzard said WoW: Forever was the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history by peak concurrent players, and that it had brought in the highest number of returning players the game has ever seen.

Longdale added at the time that it had pulled in the most newly introduced players for a WoW launch in 15 years. It has since suffered its first controversy, though, with a now-fixed gold exploit.

Last week, players pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. At the time of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among newly introduced and returning players.

Despite No Disc, GTA 6 Recorded the UK's Biggest Physical Launch Since 2019

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 has been breaking records all over the place, so it doesn't come as much of a surprise to learn that its performance at physical retail has been mighty impressive.
  • As reported by The Game Business, based on data from UK tracker Nielsen IQ, GTA 6 has recorded the country's largest physical launch since 2019's FIFA 20.
  • GTA 6's physical sales generated £32 million in revenue in its first three days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has been breaking records all over the place, so it doesn't come as much of a surprise to learn that its performance at physical retail has been mighty impressive.

As reported by The Game Business, based on data from UK tracker Nielsen IQ, GTA 6 has recorded the country's largest physical launch since 2019's FIFA 20. Turns out only the nation's love of football can compete.

GTA 6's physical sales generated £32 million in revenue in its first three days. Apparently, it's the 17th biggest physical launch in the UK ever.

That might not sound particularly grand, but if you consider how much the physical market has shrunk over the last few years, it's actually pretty remarkable.

All this has transpired despite the game's physical copies coming with a download code rather than a disc, something that caused some anguish among collectors and enthusiasts.

I think it maybe proves that people will still show up for a physical product, even in a world where discs are on their way out.

PlayStation plans to discontinue making discs for its platform starting in 2028, but it's possible we'll still see physical releases for major games — just with a code in the box instead of a Blu-ray.

Anyway, GTA 6 has been selling well on all fronts, surprise surprise. Did you pick up the physical version of the game? Tell us in the comments section below.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • CyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game introduced, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site.
  • Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB.
  • In a recent development, "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game introduced, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This newly introduced leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

In a recent development, "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek states the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

It has been revealed that what does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

"If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

CyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.
