That last point's a bit of contention in the community, given hunters are out-performing other classes in damage, but given we're just three weeks into the game with a couple of weeks left to go before the raid tier, I'm not sweating the lack of an immediate nerf bat.

In a recent development, right, there's my journalistic obligation taken care of. Here's why I'm (not) upset.

It has been revealed that scarlet Subterfuge—and In Dreams—is widely considered one of the crappiest quests in Classic, and given this is a game that's already rife with inconvenience—inconvenience I am usually all for—that's saying something. In it, you need to go and find Highlord Taelan Fordring, son of Tirion Fordring, and remove the scarlet-coloured wool from his eyes.

Industry observers note that story-wise, this quest kicks ass. You're finding the son of the guy who wielded the Ashbringer. Realising his life has been a lie, he hulks out, cleaving down his former scarlet allies, and marches out of the fortress side-by-side with you. Mechanically, it sucks so much, dude.

To reach Fordring the younger, you need to go halfway across the zone, talk to an illusionist hermit, and don a disguise. Then you need to jog all the way up to where Taelan is to give him the news.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The only downside is that this disguise lasts for 30 minutes, and escorting Taelan, at least with the current strategy (more on this later) lasts for about 20 minutes. And if you don't have the disguise on, he's hostile to you, even if you're just restarting the escort quest. So that means that if anybody else is doing the quest by the time you get there, you need to either:.

The actual escort is annoying, too: Since Taelan can technically handle the Scarlet Crusade on his lonesome, accepted practice for this quest has been to simply let him handle things. Which both makes it take ages and makes it difficult to find a group so that you can do it the intended way.

In a recent development, as a cherry on top, you can't really skip this quest outright as it gives some really powerful pre-BiS endgame items. Still, I persevered, I did it yesterday, and Blizzard, uh. Blizzard gave the disguise an hour-long duration literally today.

"Western Plaguelands - The Scarlet Illusion granted during the quest 'Scarlet Subterfuge' now lasts an hour (was 30 minutes).".

It has been revealed that this doesn't make the quest any less of a headache to finish, but hey—at least if someone else is already doing it, you won't have to jog back to your hag friend or play the log-in, log-out Hokey Pokey until he respawns. Good for you.

In a recent development, if you want your Nintendo Switch 2 to sound as good as possible, you won't dream of using the handheld's built-in stereo speakers, and will pick up a headset to use with the system. It won't cost you much to do so, with Black Friday deals cutting cost on gaming-designed headphones.

Recent findings suggest that there are loads of Black Friday gaming headset deals at Currys, with the best reducing models down to lovely tempting prices. Some are discounted to below £50, which means they're cheaper than the cost of a Switch 2 game. They're all wired models, as cable-toting tech is generally cheaper, which means these options still offer some impressive specs despite the low price. In particular there are four headsets below this price threshold which work on the Switch 2, and you can find them below, ordered from cheapest to priciest.

In a recent development, this wired Logitech gaming headset is over 50% off, despite its specs. It offers 7.1 sound, and is certified as a DTS Headphone:X headphone. It's pretty simple in terms of features, but it's a simple way of getting wired audio from your Switch (or any other console).

Sources indicate that this gaming headset is roughly a year old, so is starting to see discounts. It gives you an affordable way to experience some of Turtle Beach's popular audio features, and it's pretty lightweight compared to rivals too.

Industry observers note that hyperX offers a fair few gaming headsets we recommend, but thanks to the discount, this is perhaps the cheapest. It's surprisingly cheap when you consider it has dual drivers, offering sonic nuance many alternatives miss.

Sources indicate that coming just under the £50 threshold is this alternative HyperX model, which has a wider range of connection options than the above model and has a more durable frame. It's also designed to be comfortable with soft leatherette padding and memory foam cushions.

Recent findings suggest that the main appeal of almost any gaming headset is thus: dedicated cans will sound better than the tinny loudspeakers you get in a handheld console. The presence of a proper microphone is a benefit too, if you play online with people.

If you usually play your Switch 2 on your home TV, while it's docked, you might not therefore need a gaming headset. Maybe your TV's built-in speakers, or the loudspeakers or soundbar you use for it, work just as well.

I'd therefore recommend a headset mostly to people who play their Switch 2 on the go. In many situations, you can't play your Switch out loud in the first place, so a headset is crucial, especially since all cans block out surrounding noise by virtue of their padded ear cushions.

Industry observers note that but what about cheap versus expensive headsets? Honestly, I think pricey cans are best suited to competitive esports players who need to hear everything around them, or PC gamers who'll have much better access to the headphone software. Usually, what you're paying for is an elite roster of tools, features and preset EQ modes, and it's often hard to play around with those tools if you're not on a computer.

So for most buyers, a budget pair of cans like this is perfect, because audio quality is often the one thing you're not compromising on. The only thing you might want, that costs more, is a wireless connection. If you don't like the idea of using a physical cable, maybe you should pay a little bit more, but convenience is the only benefit to a Bluetooth connection in gaming headsets.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Persona 6 is still slowly chugging in the background, but developer Atlus is promising that future games in its beloved RPG series won't take quite as long as they used to.

There was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped. Despite the sometimes agonising wait filled with countless spin-offs and collaborations with live service games, we've only seen a vague teaser trailer for the next proper Persona.

Recent findings suggest that P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada recently assured folks that the pattern wouldn't repeat again. "Persona 6 is not the end," he mentioned in a Sega Samania interview translated by GamesRadar. "We have been working to make sure that people won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously. In order for Persona to grow as an IP, we consider how to live up to people's expectations in terms of creativity and development every day.".

Recent findings suggest that wada doesn't go into any more detail about how Atlus plans to release Persona games quicker. Is the next mainline game already in development alongside Persona 6, or is Atlus just streamlining how it makes games? Either way, the studio seems to have abandoned its divisive habit of returning to and improving its games after a few years - P3 Portable, P4 Golden, P5 Royal. I imagine that'll cut down on wait times, at least somewhat.

"Large-scale RPGs like the Persona series take five years or more to develop," he added. "So there can be a long time between numbered entries.".

As for Persona 6 itself, Wada unsurprisingly "can't say much" about the much-hyped, high-schooling, demon-punching game. "But we want our games to demonstrate all of the hard work we've put in. With that in mind, we are creating something better than anything we've made before, and that is hugely satisfying.".

Recent findings suggest that we don't know much about Atlus' occult sequel, officially, but a massive information leak earlier in the year revealed a full achievement list for Persona 6 and a bunch of other unreleased games, including Kingdom Hearts 4 and an unannounced Sea of Thieves project. Be wary of online spoilers, then.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Surprise, surprise - GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing its predecessor's 13-year-long record and the already optimistic analyst estimates.

Rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November. By the end of its first day on sale, GTA 6 managed to rake in a frankly absurd $3.79bn. Not a bad haul.

As Rockstar was quick to brag, the whopping performance means GTA 6 set "a new record for entertainment across any medium" by "becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.".

For context, GTA 5 made around $800m in its opening 24 hours more than a decade ago. That mammoth debut almost looks quaint next to GTA 6's stunning numbers, although it's notable GTA 5 didn't launch immediately in Japan or Brazil - GTA 6 is available in almost every market with access to PlayStation and Xbox consoles.

"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," said Rockstar co-founder and company president, Sam Houser, in a recent press release. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you.".

It has been revealed that previous estimates guessed that GTA 6 had sold almost 25m copies ($2.5bn in revenue) on day one. It's fair to say the game's staggering performance blew even those sky-high projections out of the water.

Every early indicator pointed to GTA 6's inevitably record-breaking launch. Parent company Take-Two previously said the game was tracking "well above expectations," as the crime fest sold more pre-orders than any other game in PlayStation Store and Xbox Store history.

The only question now is whether GTA 6 can ever outsell GTA 5's mammoth 230m copies, which it reached thanks to a very healthy cadence of GTA Online updates. How high GTA 6 can go will likely depend on its multiplayer offering, though Rockstar hasn't said anything concrete about that just yet.

"A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," Chris Tapsell gushed in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Facepunch Studios continue to work on S&box, the mix of open source game development platform and Garry's Mod spiritual successor they released to mixed reviews earlier this year.
  • "This latest system isn't really new," Newman wrote.
  • According to recent reports, similarly, in terms of the updated sandbox mode, Newman noted he feels the team have been "walking the line of making a more modern Garry's Mod really well".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Facepunch Studios continue to work on S&box, the mix of open source game development platform and Garry's Mod spiritual successor they released to mixed reviews earlier this year. That rough start has it in need of a redemption arc, which the Rust devs are hoping will be powered by going free-to-play and making changes like the revamp of sandbox mode they've just rolled out.

"This latest system isn't really new," Newman wrote. "It's the exact same system that Garry's Mod uses. I hold my hands up here, I thought that spawning from the cloud was better...but I was wrong. There definitely is something a lot nicer about installing a massive model pack and then having everything right there. I'm sorry it took me so long to come around to realising this.".

According to recent reports, similarly, in terms of the updated sandbox mode, Newman noted he feels the team have been "walking the line of making a more modern Garry's Mod really well". "I'm excited by all the possibilities of it," he continued. "Obviously there aren't a ton of addons right now but what we do have is showing a LOT of potential, and that's only going to grow. I've been going through improving things that feel outdated or stupid. I'm resisting bending it all too far, I want it to stay kind of familiar for everyone, but I think we can improve a few things in our new engine.".

A number of old school sandbox props, such as chunks of robotics, wheels, gears, and hunks of steel girder are on their way back, while Facepunch are finally ready to add in water. "It has waves," Newman wrote of the latter. "The physics objects get tossed around in the waves. You can go underwater, and swim, and there's caustics and fog and particles and post process effects and stuff." Also, NPCs now "live directly in the engine" making it easier to set up a fight club.

A simplified menu and a whole bunch of performance and dev-focused tweaks round out this patch, so go through the full notes if you're keen to read about the likes of workshop mounts and VRAM fragmentation.

As of writing, S&box is still yet to go free-to-play, a change Newman and co previously mentioned is coming "towards the end of the year". If it can nail recapturing the classic GMod magic with updates that players actually want, I think it stands a chance of a comeback. However, as its lifespan thus far has proven, it's harder to rely on high quality user-made games within a game than ever before in an age when people can just resort to using generative AI for an ever-increasing number of things.

  • It has been revealed that for years it seemed like seeing the X-Men and Avengers together was a pipe dream, but Disney's acquisition of 20th Century Fox opened the door for it to finally happen.
  • It has been revealed that press for the next Avengers movie is underway, with the final Doomsday trailer arriving just days ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it's a very exciting time in the Marvel Cinematic Universe! We're just weeks away from the upcoming Marvel movie Avengers: Doomsday hitting theaters, which features a thrilling crossover with four teams of superheroes. That includes the Avengers and the OG stars of the X-Men movies teaming up for the first time on the big screen. Studio boss Kevin Feige recently referenced comments Hugh Jackman made back in the day about this long-awaited moment, and we tracked down the interview.

It has been revealed that for years it seemed like seeing the X-Men and Avengers together was a pipe dream, but Disney's acquisition of 20th Century Fox opened the door for it to finally happen. It turns out that long before joining the MCU in Deadpool & Wolverine, Hugh Jackman had hoped to see these teams together on the big screen. Let's break it all down.

It has been revealed that press for the next Avengers movie is underway, with the final Doomsday trailer arriving just days ago. During a recent interview with Empire, Kevin Feige spoke about bringing the X-Men and the Avengers (plus the Upcoming Avengers and Fantastic Four) together for the highly anticipated blockbuster. He referenced the Greatest Showman actor by saying:.

In a recent development, you see interviews of Hugh Jackman 15, 20 years ago saying, ‘People say it’s impossible, but maybe someday the X-Men and the Avengers can all get together.' It just felt right. It just felt like the fun way to culminate a quarter-century of storytelling.

Industry observers note that he's not wrong. The MCU has been going strong since back in 2008, but for years it was noticeably missing beloved Marvel characters like Spider-Man, the Fantastic Four, and the X-Men. The latter had its own series of live-action movies for 19 years, which took place separate from Marvel's shared universe. Those worlds are finally colliding in Avengers: Doomsday, to the joy of fans who have been following the respective properties for well over two decades.

Of course, we had to track down the comments from Jackman that Kevin Feige was referencing to the outlet. They actually date back in 2013.

Hugh Jackman spoke about wanting to see this crossover over a decade ago (2013 to be exact), while promoting his spinoff The Wolverine in an interview with Collider (via YouTube). While Marvel characters were spread across three different studios, the Oscar-nominated actor mentioned the following:.

According to recent reports, I believe, maybe I'm optimistic, I understand the Marvel has The Avengers, they have a lot of major things going on. But at some point, I just find it almost impossible to believe there's not a way to bring Iron Man and all the Avengers characters to Wolverine, the X-Men characters, Spider-Man and somehow get them in together.

Turns out, he was right on the money. Of course, it took some extenuating circumstances to allow for this crossover to finally happen. Namely, Disney acquiring Fox, as well as the studio forming a joint custody agreement with Sony regarding Tom Holland's Spider-Man. It might have taken an additional 10 years, but we're finally getting the chance to see the Avengers and X-Men on the silver screen together this December.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

In the same interview, Jackman addressed the legal headache involved in the possible crossover.

I don't see the impediment. I'm like 'OK, you've got three studios. Just split it three ways in terms of costs. And Happy Days, it's all coming together.

Sources indicate that doomsday has clearly been a long time coming, which should presumably result in massive box office numbers and (hopefully) positive word of mouth. We'll have to see how it all shakes out, but the hype surrounding the project is VERY high. Unfortunately, Jackman wasn't included in the Doomsday cast announcement. Also--Kevin Feige teased more surprise characters being included, and maybe he'll even surprise us and pop up in The Russo Brothers' movie. Fingers crossed for some unexpected moments.

Review: Zero Parades: Director's Cut (PS5) - A Riveting Spy Thriller That Still Lacks Disco Elysium's Bite

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1371 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I’m on sub-level three of a long-abandoned rocket silo, reading heavily redacted files by flashlight.
  • Sources indicate that it’s not flashy nor is it a massive spectacle, and it’s taken me hours to get to this point.
  • This game is Zero Parades: Director’s Cut, the spiritual successor to ZA/UM’s enormously praised Disco Elysium, which has finally made its way to PS5 after launching on PC earlier in 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I’m on sub-level three of a long-abandoned rocket silo, reading heavily redacted files by flashlight. Most of the screen is black, save for a little pang of light from my torch, and my heart beats rapidly as I comb through reams of text on the right of the screen.

Sources indicate that it’s not flashy nor is it a massive spectacle, and it’s taken me hours to get to this point. However, it may be one of the most engrossing gaming moments I’ve had on PS5 this year.

This game is Zero Parades: Director’s Cut, the spiritual successor to ZA/UM’s enormously praised Disco Elysium, which has finally made its way to PS5 after launching on PC earlier in 2026.

It’s a text-and-dice-based RPG, where Operant (read: spy) Cascade has returned to the town of Portofiro five years after an assignment went horribly wrong. This is her chance at redemption.

However, upon arriving in Portofiro, she finds her double comatose in their safe house, and with no clue as to what her assignment actually is, Cascade must take to the streets.

Industry observers note that what you’ll find there is a massive, sprawling collection of mysteries that weave and connect in myriad ways. A girl’s plea to help find her missing dad may link to a poetry magazine that could be a front. A cosmonaut figure in the bustling bazaar was my first thread that eventually led me to read through documents underground in the dark 20 hours later.

Admittedly, there are times that pacing is to its detriment. The opening hours are especially slow, as you get a lay of the land. However, like any good mystery thriller, I'm of the opinion you have to put in the time before you can reap those mysterious rewards. It's not going to be for everyone — which should be obvious with the whole text-and-dice-based RPG descriptor — however, if it is your thing, then your patience will pay off.

Recent findings suggest that zero Parades is a familiar game for anyone that played Disco Elysium, but it does have its own unique identity. There’s a lot of crossover, from the style of narration to the stacked-against-you odds of its dice-driven actions. However, where Disco is a more internal reflection of our initially nameless detective, Zero Parades sprinkles some of that in with a deal more narrative mystery, and I love that about it.

It has been revealed that cascade is basically a f*ck up, haunted by the elusive errors of her past, so while you may have the skill somewhere inside of you to be a good spy, it’s but a fleeting thing. It’s entirely down to how you level up Cascade, across the faculties of action, relation, and intelligence to define the kind of spy you are.

Kicking off my investigation, I pile a ton of points into intelligence skill, particularly Technoflex, the study of all things tech. Sometimes this skill is subtly useful, like being able to fix the fax machine in the photo printing store where my safe house is located. Other times, it proves its worth in big ways, like being able to bypass the security lock of a secret prison, because I am aware of a system flaw in that precise model.

However, there is real flexibility to Zero Parades’ exploration and progression. For example, that secret prison has multiple ways in, and you may be able to talk yourself in via the front door if you have the right skills levelled up.

By the time you figure out your assignment, the narrative has laid the foundation for many different approaches, and each can take you on its own weird road through the streets of Portofiro, and your success down those roads is dependent on how you build up your character.

It has been revealed that and let me be clear: you can simply fail in Zero Parades – it’s sort of the crux of the whole experience. Whether it’s a botched escape from a mysterious man, or completely messing up an attempt to construct a homemade gun, Zero Parades is brilliant at making it feel like the odds are stacked against you.

According to recent reports, that is emphasised all the more with the stress system. Across fatigue, anxiety, and delirium (which relate to your action, relation, and intelligence upgrades), certain actions will build up pressure in any three of these gauges. As it ascends, Cascade will be hit with nerfs of varying severity, and if the scale maxes out, it will refresh and deduct a skill point for its related skill group.

There are ways to juggle this, of course. Smoking cigarettes, eating sweets, or certain drinks can lower specific gauges whilst increasing others, and sleeping is possible to reduce all gauges but is time-locked. You are then able to exert yourself to increase the chances of hitting the required dice numbers, but this comes at the cost of increasing the scale of its related gauge.

Recent findings suggest that the whole experience becomes a balancing act while trying to figure out which gauge may still require space to carry out certain actions. Maybe you decide not to engage in some activity for fear of needing it in something more crucial. Or maybe you spend it all wanting to cover everything, and then suffer the consequences when you really need it in a pivotal story moment.

This whole system means I am vehemently aware of Cascade’s physical and mental state at pretty much all times across the story. It also means that no part of the game’s content is trivial, as it all ties into one and other, not just narratively but mechanically. What I do now directly impacts what I can do later.

By the time the credits rolled, my ending felt especially my own. My own failures, successes, and regrets. And it massively encourages me to go for another try, to hopefully unlock newly introduced avenues, level up in different areas, and maybe even finish successfully (I messed up badly).

Recent findings suggest that as you can tell, I am a big fan of this game, but it doesn’t get everything right. For one, the writing is great, as you would hope for, but it lacks the same razor edge that Disco Elysium has in spades. Voice acting is generally brilliant, but at times it feels like a game doing its best Disco impression, with a yearning to be as edgy as possible.

I did come to like Cascade’s voice performance a lot more as I spent more time with it, but it undeniably lacks the same punch as Lenvel Brown’s dulcet tones as The Narrator in Disco Elysium.

Sources indicate that then we come to the PS5’s performance. I played this on both PS5 and PS5 Pro, and the performance is surprisingly bad. For 90% of the game, as you talk to various characters, it’s obviously not an glitch – you’re mainly just looking at still screens as text moves down the right side. However, when you’re running around the town of Portofiro, the frame rate consistently tanks.

It’s a shame because the art style is quite gorgeous, as it somehow mixes a painterly art style with a simultaneously dull aesthetic. Like in the story, Portofiro is a town of stalled potential, left to rot over its beauty. DualSense haptics are also surprisingly great, albeit subtle. It really makes you feel like you're flicking through redacted documents with nuanced ripples at your fingertips.

In a recent development, zero Parades: Director’s Cut is a dense and highly detailed text-based RPG, that moves at a painstakingly slow pace. However, it’s part of the magic of this story. It lacks the same authenticity as Disco Elysium, but manages to hold its own with a riveting mystery that very naturally unfolds.

It’s riveting when a small detail links back to the previously abandoned thread, and you feel like a spy yourself as you try to piece it all together. It lets you relish in the world and revel in the chaos, and as the credits rolled, I just wanted to jump back in and try it all over again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 features the first non-binary character in the series' history, according to actor Jesse James Rose, who plays the role of a museum curator in the game.

"I can FINALLY share that I play the first-ever nonbinary character in the Grand Theft Auto franchise!" Rose wrote on Instagram.

"Absolutely wild to find out THIS was the super-secret game I spent weeks and 17 NDAs filming 3 years ago.".

In a recent development, "I shot this back in my they/them days, and everyone on production ensured I was comfortable and gendered correctly," Rose wrote. The project was kept so secret that Rose wasn't told what it was during filming and only recently learned it was GTA 6.

"GTA was one of the most inclusive & caring sets I've ever been on," they added.

A post shared by Jesse James Rose ✨ (@jamesissmiling).

According to recent reports, the role was shot entirely through motion capture, which meant wearing "a unitard made of dots every day". Rose also says steps were taken to protect the character in-game: "To mitigate anti-trans violence, I was assured that players would not be able to inflict violence against my character.".

It has been revealed that A whole day of the shoot was spent scanning Rose's face, including hours of pulling different expressions. At one point Rose couldn't move a particular muscle, and worried the scan had been ruined, but the director was thrilled.

"That right there is exactly why we'll never use AI," he remarked, according to Rose. "A computer could never come up with the face you just made.".

"Remember, in a world consumed with Generative AI, the largest video game in history chose human labour to preserve the integrity of the game," Rose added.

Rose did raise some concerns about pay, though.

"Despite being paid well for my time on set, I'll never see a residual check for my work," Rose wrote, explaining that this is part of SAG’s contract with game developers. As a union leader at one of SAG's sister unions, Rose noted there's still "a long way to go to ensure arts workers are fairly compensated for our labour".

In a recent development, rose also claims many other trans people worked on GTA 6, both in front of the camera and behind it. "SO many trans people besides me are featured in GTA VI as other roles, designers, writers, etc... take a note, theatre and TV! We are employable & profitable!!!".

Sources indicate that finally, Rose voiced support for Rockstar's UK staff. "UK-based workers at Rockstar Games are currently voting on whether to unionise, and I sincerely hope their efforts are successful," Rose wrote. "Every arts worker should have a stable job with benefits and fair working conditions protected by a union.".

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is out now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It launched on Thursday, although some have been getting in on the action earlier, as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even Newly introduced Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Grand Theft Auto 6 might be one of the best-reviewed games of all time, but you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score.

It has been revealed that while critics have given Rockstar's latest a Metascore of 99, its user score has dropped to 5.6 out of 10 at the time of writing, which Metacritic classifies as "mixed or average". Of the 54,000+ ratings left, 44 percent are "negative".

The score had previously dropped into the red, but has since recovered a little.

Some negative reviews raise genuine complaints, such as the game's 30FPS cap on console, while others take issue with how much of the story focuses on Jason and Lucia's relationship instead of the crime-spree antics of past games.

In a recent development, "Expectations might've killed this game," states one 0/10 review. "The hype that something otherworldly would come to be flopped. The hyperrealism makes it feel slow, mundane and boring. Its a tecnichal [sic] advancement for sure but for the wrong reasons. Goodlooks zero personality type stuff. Its not as edgy as the rest of the gta games. And thats exactly my problem like is not funny. The game gets carried by its visuals and radio stations. Certain limitations make it feel like not gta and latest features make it feel like not gta. In the end it feels like a life simulator and the point of gaming is to escape from reality.".

"Genuinely hated almost every minute of this experience," wrote another. "After years of waiting and an absurd amount of hype, GTA VI somehow managed to leave me more frustrated than entertained. The excessive sexual content gets exhausting, and instead of adding anything meaningful to the experience, it often feels like Rockstar is desperately trying to shock its audience.

Industry observers note that "The story is painfully disappointing, the writing fails to keep me invested, and I honestly couldn't care less about what happens to most of these **** gameplay isn't doing the game any favours either. Glitches, bugs, annoying inconsistencies, and frustrating moments constantly get in the way of actually enjoying the experience. It's ridiculous that a game of this scale, backed by a studio with Rockstar's resources, can feel this rough. I expected a polished experience, not a glorified debugging ****.".

Others point to "woke" and "DEI" agendas.

"A major step down in the writing department compared to previous instalments coupled with the obvious DEI-fication, unfun realism and the resulting player freedom restrictions leave a sour taste in the otherwise detailed gorgeous open world," said one reviewer. Another unhappy player wrote: "Shameful DEI hijacked cuck simulator, the most overrated game of all time and it's not even close.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Analyst estimates have put GTA 6 at 53 million copies sold, which, if accurate, places it as the 13th best-selling game of all time after just a week.

In the least surprising bit of news of 2026, GTA 6 is selling pretty well. It was probably the most anticipated game ever and is the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic, so naturally the sales have followed. The first official number from Rockstar Games placed it at 32.5 million copies sold before it was even released, which had made it the 30th best-selling game ever above the likes of Super Mario Odyssey, Monster Hunter World, and Elden Ring. But that was just pre-release, so it's no shock to say that its fortunes haven't ended there.

Alinea Analytics' head of market analysis, Rhys Elliott, posts the latest estimate over on Twitter, which places Rockstar's latest at 53 million copies sold, making $4.7 billion in its first week.

If this number is accurate, GTA 6 is the 13th best-selling game ever, with it unseating Animal Crossing: Fresh Horizons, and overtaking the likes of Cyberpunk 2077, The Sims, and the Pokemon Generation 1 games (which have a combined sales figure of 47.44 million across Red, Blue and Yellow).

It has been revealed that GTA 6 has sold 53M copies (75.7% on PS5) after a week on the market (@alineaanalytics estimates). Some other quick stats from our estimates: - It's made $4.7B (76.1% on PS5, due to regional prices) - 7M players have already played for over 50 hours. - 250K folks have played for over 100 hours (!!!!) - The US accounts for 33.5% of PS5's GTA 6 copies. Publishing another substantial deep dive on Substack shortly.November 27, 2026.

Elliott's data also estimates that just under a quarter of GTA 6 sales were on Xbox, with the Series X|S version accounting for 13 million vs PS5's 40 million. And it's not like it's just selling well either, as he reckons that seven million players have already played over 50 hours, with 250k of those having already played 100 hours. For reference, the game had been out in New Zealand around 219 hours at the time the tweet was posted.

Obviously, this is massively impressive no matter how you look at it. But it's worth keeping in mind that the PC release hasn't even dropped yet, so this has the potential to skyrocket once more when PC players – and console players who are going to double dip – get their hands on it.

Revision [Fri 27th Nov 2026, 4:32pm]:.

Digital Foundry's John Linneman has also weighed in on this:.

Original Story: Yesterday, we published an article about how Xbox fans were making their voices heard regarding a lack of Definitive Edition upgrade for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair, and we've now got an official statement about it.

In a post on social media, developer Playtonic Games explained that "the cost of bringing it to more platforms just isn't viable for us at this time", and that they've had to "prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs".

Here's the full statement that was shared by the studio:.

"Hi folks, just wanted to say a massive thanks to everyone on here for the support for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition. The response has BEE-n incredible, and we can't wait for you to experience the game all over again on December 15th. We are aware of feedback regarding the lack of Xbox Series S/X support, and we just wanted to provide some clarity on the reasoning behind this decision.

In a recent development, bringing Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition to PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 has been an exciting adventure, and we can't wait for latest and returning players alike to experience the Impossible Lair on these platforms for the first time. Unfortunately, we've had to prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future.

Sources indicate that we understand the frustration felt by those of you who won't be able to access the Definitive Edition at launch, but unfortunately the cost of bringing it to more platforms just isn't viable for us at this time. As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face. Please know that this wasn't an easy decision to make, and we apologise to any of you affected by this. We only wish things were different, and we value every single one of you and your feedback.".

Based on this, it only sounds like there's a slim chance of getting the Definitive Edition upgrade of Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair on Xbox, but who knows whether it could end up being added down the line.

For what it's worth, the game already runs and plays well on Xbox One, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S, but it's obviously a bummer when other platforms are getting enhanced visuals and up to 120FPS as part of this upgrade.

It is what it is! We'll just keep enjoying the 2019 version instead.

What are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

Tech Report: "More than just war and peace": Total War: Medieval 3's diplomacy system will build on Three Kingdoms' backstabbing, with rulers who aren't just focused on you

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (763 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Creative Assembly's Total War: Medieval 3 is going to do a lot more with diplomacy, the developers promise.
  • Specifically, Creative Assembly want to create a sense of factions with autonomous agendas and evolving intentions, while placing more stress on questions of geography.
  • In a blog, game director Pawel Wojs hails Three Kingdoms as "a game defined by its dynamic use of diplomacy, where coalitions, alliances and relationships between characters and factions could fundamentally change the course of a campaign." He continues: "We want to build on those foundations, taking what worked well and exploring how we can push it further for the Medieval world.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Creative Assembly's Total War: Medieval 3 is going to do a lot more with diplomacy, the developers promise. Diplomacy! The soul of any Total War game. They're going to build on the example of Total War: Three Kingdoms, which does allow for some gratifying backroom dealing, in fairness. During my first Thringdoms runthrough, I played Cao Cao, a ruler gifted with the ability to hypnotise people into liking him while hating each other. I spent many idle hours instigating proxy wars. Medieval 3 is apparently going to take all that to "new heights". It is going to make Han politicking seem as sophisticated as texting "get your filthy hands off my bae" to everybody you know on Valentine's Day.

Specifically, Creative Assembly want to create a sense of factions with autonomous agendas and evolving intentions, while placing more stress on questions of geography.

In a blog, game director Pawel Wojs hails Three Kingdoms as "a game defined by its dynamic use of diplomacy, where coalitions, alliances and relationships between characters and factions could fundamentally change the course of a campaign." He continues: "We want to build on those foundations, taking what worked well and exploring how we can push it further for the Medieval world.".

It has been revealed that as regards "believable agendas", Creative Assemble want the campaign AI to display both a survival instinct and the ability to "pursue its own interests instead of primarily being an antagonist to the player". These agendas will span the game's Politics, Economy, and Families systems, with dynastic considerations affecting behaviour. They want you to be able to read another ruler's intent by tracking back through their past actions. They want weaker factions to sue for peace or seek sensible alliances, rather than "stubbornly being entrenched in a war it is bound to lose". Aww, but I love it when Scotland does that.

The game will aim for a balance of long-term thinking and opportunism, with AI leaders pouncing on short-term prospects even as they keep the whole in mind. And then there are inconvenient "ripple effects": you might get involved with a neighbouring succession crisis because you don't want to deal with the fallout if, you know, That Guy takes the throne.

According to recent reports, speaking of borders, Creative Assembly also want would-be treaty-makers to think harder about terrain and transportation. "For example: You finally reach a faraway realm with your diplomat, opening diplomatic relations to a realm far beyond your initial sphere of influence," Wojs goes on. "Relations are positive, but meaningless due to the lack of physical proximity. Once that faraway realm has access to a port, a trade route can finally be established. This leads to an exchange in culture and trade, and may finally allow you to recruit foreign units into your service.".

I have to say, I do find a lot of this language either broadly familiar from previous Twars, or too general to reveal much. There is, however, a closing in-game anecdote from principal designer Thomas Schut that digs into the detail. Schut gives the example of you sending a diplomat to negotiate a 10 year non-aggression pact greased by recognition of another ruler's royal title, in return for their vassalage. Sending a diplomat allows you to negotiate on the spot, but if you'd rather not spare a diplomat, you can also dispatch sealed letters at the price of not being able to see and respond immediately to the other faction's reaction.

Sources indicate that rulers can make public claims to cities, calling on other rulers to support them. Simply conquering and annexing them will damage your standing in every court. You can also forge claims to cities, if only as insurance against wanting to own them someday. Get enough rulers to back you, and you'll be able to throw around grander pronouncements about what you're divinely entitled to. You are the Emperor of Everything! Coalitions will apparently form and fragment over years, old friends turning on each other as their dark plots come to light.

Sources indicate that the joy of Cao Cao puppetry notwithstanding, I don't play Total War for the chance to thrash out cunning pacts with bots. I am here to put my archers behind my spearfolk - and hope the other side's cavalry don't notice the cutthroats I've stationed in the woods. I'm more interested in what I've read about Medieval 3's regional levies system. Still, it does sound like Creative Assembly are serious about giving you things to do besides putting other wannabe kings to the sword.

Some Grand Theft Auto 6 players on PS5 say the game keeps crashing with error code CE-108255-1, and in some cases, it's stopping them from progressing through the story.

"The game runs perfectly fine for a while. I can complete missions and chapters without any issues, but then it suddenly crashes after around 40 minutes and sends me back to the PS5 home screen", wrote one Reddit user. They added that other games, including GTA 5 and For Honor, run without crashing.

Another player told Dexerto that GTA 6 worked fine until Pipework, an early mission that introduces Mandy, but now crashes "every time I use the plunger or stand around the sink with it", which means they can’t progress.

Some PS5 Pro owners say the game crashes during the opening prologue, either at the same point every time or a few seconds in, and they haven't been able to play since launch.

Others say they've tried the usual fixes, such as clearing their console's cache, rebuilding the database, factory resetting their PS5, and even downloading the game three times, but nothing has worked thus far.

It's not just PS5 players that are struggling, either; some Xbox Series X players have reported crashes too, with one saying the game sometimes crashes after just 15 minutes.

Rockstar hasn't yet acknowledged the crashes or noted whether a patch is on the way, and its own support is sending players with console errors to PlayStation or Xbox directly for help.

In a recent development, unfortunately, there's no firm fix just yet. PlayStation's support page describes CE-108255-1 simply as "an error occurred with the game/application”, and its only advice is to "try updating your game". Highlight GTA 6 on your home screen, press Options, and choose Check for Patch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I watched my first season of Dancing with the Stars this year, and the journey has definitely been a doozy. After tuning in to the competition show on ABC, I was shaken up by the twists and turns that came, including the power of the fan vote that resulted in both Jenna Dewan and Harry Shum Jr. being eliminated ahead of the finale. It turns out that finalist Connor Wood joked about being portrayed as a villain prior to Ezra Frech's historic win.

It has been revealed that there was a ton of discourse about DWTS during its last few episodes, with pro Sharna Burgess slamming how fan votes factor in. Plenty of folks online were mad about Wood staying on, while (what many felt were) superior dancers like Harry and Jenna got eliminated. During an interview with THR prior to the finale, Connor spoke about the fan perception of him, offering:.

The rest of the internet, totally different story right now. We’ve gotten to a point where I have become a bit of a villain for some people.

Industry observers note that obviously, Connor didn't do anything actually villainous, but his getting through to the Dancing with the Stars finale was a shock for many viewers out there, especially when you compared his performances to those of other contestants. His placement seemed to be entirely due to fan votes, since Wood had the lowest scores in the final weeks of the show. Some fans were worried about whether or not underdog Tatyana Ali would stay in the competition, which ended up resulting in Connor becoming the "villain" of the seasons.

Clearly, the fan vote on Dancing with the Stars is important, but it can also seemingly create more division and drama for those watching the acclaimed reality TV series. Later in the same interview, Wood spoke more about this perception as a contestant, offering:.

According to recent reports, I think that they think that I personally voted their favorite off, and it’s like — I’m aware of my level of dance skill. I have nothing to do with me staying here. That’s just been just the dark side of making it as far as we made it. My understanding is that the more that people go home, the more the fans of those people will go to someone else’s page and villainize those people. That’s sad, and it’s just a testament to how invested people are in this show.

Sources indicate that in the end, Connor would end up in third place on Dancing with the Stars Season 35, beating fellow finalists Maura Higgins and Tatyana Ali. I can only imagine how his "villain" persona might have been amplified if he managed to place even better... especially if he ended up beating Ezra as the winner taking home the Mirrorball trophy this season.

In a recent development, ultimately the final two pairs of the season were Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov, as well as Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach. The latter would end up going home with the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy, following a viral final performance where the paralympic athlete's prosthetic leg came off mid-performance. It was a truly epic moment, especially when he managed to overcome it and finish the final dance with his partner.

I thought Ezra was deserving of a win before this final dance, but after seeing the way he overcame and finished the performance, the idea of Connor somehow beating both him and Amber was cringeworthy. In the end that didn't happen, and hopefully Wood can shake off his villain status as more time passes.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Phasmophobia's next upgrade, Resonance, arrives on 24th November, bringing a brand-new piece of ghost-hunting kit, more voice commands, and a move to the Unity 6 engine.
  • The headline addition is dowsing rods, which will help you track down the bone, making them particularly handy on bigger maps like Brownstone High School.
  • The Sound Sensor is getting an overhaul too, with a reworked interface to help you work out where sounds are coming from.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Phasmophobia's next upgrade, Resonance, arrives on 24th November, bringing a brand-new piece of ghost-hunting kit, more voice commands, and a move to the Unity 6 engine.

The headline addition is dowsing rods, which will help you track down the bone, making them particularly handy on bigger maps like Brownstone High School. As with the rest of the game's equipment, the higher the Tier, the more accurate the reading, and Tier 3 Dowsing Rods will pinpoint the exact floor the Bone is on.

The Sound Sensor is getting an overhaul too, with a reworked interface to help you work out where sounds are coming from. Icons will show whether a sound is ongoing or a one-off, and you'll be able to use the map to identify ghosts by how fast they move.

You'll also be able to ask ghosts to interact with doors and switches, and even throw nearby objects, with a list of usable phrases in the Journal. If you're tired of the same maps, you'll be able to build your own pool of maps to randomise from when picking a contract, and upcoming buttons let you rapidly pick small, medium, or large maps.

"We want to ensure every item in our Ghost Hunters' kits can add as much value as possible in investigations," stated Daniel Knight, CEO and game director at Kinetic Games.

"Resonance also brings Phasmophobia's move to Unity 6 - while this transition is a technical upgrade first and foremost, it has allowed us to implement major lighting improvements to make the game even more immersive.".

Alongside more realistic lighting and better stability, the switch to Unity 6 also brings expanded graphics and quality options, VR Eye Adaptation, and a suite of colour-blindness settings.

Resonance will also fix several prominent bugs, and introduce a conduct warning system that alerts players before they're banned, except in cases of severe violations.

Phasmophobia is also adding Xbox Play Anywhere support, so if you own the Xbox digital edition, you'll be able to play on Xbox Series X/S, PC, and devices like the ROG Ally.

Resonance is a free update and will be available on all platforms.

Sources indicate that phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S. It's also coming to Nintendo Switch 2, although we still don't quite know when.

Earlier this month, the Phasmophobia community raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association, more than doubling last year's total.

According to recent reports, earlier this year, Kinetic Games confirmed Phasmophobia's 1.0 launch had slipped from this year into 2027, as the studio remarked it was prioritising quality over speed following a rocky reception to its Player Character Update. The studio ended up apologising to players for complications with the long-awaited update, admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises to you".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A rating for the unannounced Nioh 3 Complete Edition has popped up on Korea's Game Rating and Administration Committee (GRAC).

As Insider Gaming spotted, the board gave Nioh 3 Complete Edition a 19+ rating on 17th November after it was submitted on 2nd November, even though Koei Tecmo hasn't announced a Complete Edition for the game yet.

The listing, translated by machine, describes it as "a compilation of additional content from the dark Sengoku action RPG Nioh 3", and gives the rating for "excessive expression of violence", noting that "red blood and body amputation frequently occur during combat".

The listing also notes an overseas rating, which Insider Gaming says is a 17+ rating from Japan's CERO.

Unlike some rating boards, GRAC publishes its ratings as soon as they're decided, which is why game listings often surface there before they're officially revealed.

Sources indicate that if Koei Tecmo follows the same pattern as Nioh 2, there may not be long to wait. GRAC's records show Nioh 2 was rated in January 2020, and its Complete Edition followed in November that year. Nioh 3 was rated on 14th November 2025, almost exactly a year ago.

According to recent reports, complete Editions typically includes the base game and all of its DLC. It could even launch alongside Nioh 3's second DLC, Bloody Insurrection, which is due in February 2027. Eurogamer has contacted Koei Tecmo for comment and we'll let you know if/when they come back to us.

Back in April, an update introduced "multiple high-difficulty Battle Scrolls" (side missions), accessible from shrines, the addition of a Stone of Penance item "which increases accessory +Values and rarities in exchange for higher difficulties", and latest skills given as rewards for completing the aforementioned high-level Battle Scroll missions.

Eurogamer's review of Nioh 3 called the threequel a new high for the 'masocore' series and "the crucible in which all of Team Ninja's experience has been siphoned into." It's sold over one million copies (and counting) since its 6th February launch.

The wait for GTA 6 was undeniably long, with 13 years passing since Rockstar's last Grand Theft Auto entry dropped and its upcoming behemoth – but fans aren't the only ones who felt the wait… those behind the game did, too.

In a recent development, especially co-protagonist Lucia's own actor, Manni L. Perez, who states she's worked on Grand Theft Auto 6 for nearly ten years now – the majority of those 13 years following GTA 5. "Life has been such a whirlwind these past couple of days and I just want to take a moment to say thank you," she writes on Instagram. "Thank you to all the newly introduced followers, to all the beautiful messages, and the positive reception the game and my character have received.".

It has been revealed that she then recalls the amount of time she's spent in Lucia's shoes: "I've dedicated almost a decade to bringing Lucia to life. She's been such a significant part of mine and I am beyond grateful she now gets to be a small part of yours." That's one heck of a role, then, considering the amount of work Perez has evidently poured into it – and I'd say it's more than paid off. As it stands, GTA 6 continues to smash records as the highest-rated game of all time.

Sources indicate that it's also already proven "the biggest launch in PlayStation history" (with Sony reporting "more than 39 million unique players" playing on just the PS5). Phew. Jason's own actor, Dylan Rourke, has posted on his profile as well, seemingly celebrating his time with Rockstar. "Thankful for this wild ride," Rourke's story reads. "Gratitude won't cut it. Make today about the ones you love. Family.".

Wild ride, indeed… and I'd say it's far from over. The community is still eagerly awaiting a PC release (and no, I'm not talking about the unofficial ports in progress), and, of course, the hotly anticipated Online counterpart. Rockstar has yet to announce either, though, but both are sure to propel GTA 6 further into relentless popularity – if you can fathom it becoming any bigger than it is now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Grand Theft Auto 6 player states they've been hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network social features ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Posting on Twitter/X on Friday evening, DerrickGott007 said they had "just got a 30-day PSN social features ban" for sending the photo, which they'd taken with the in-game camera, through PlayStation's messaging service, warning other players not to do the same.

"Do not, I repeat do not send any photos taken with the in-game camera, across the PSN messaging network that contain nudity," they wrote. "I just got a 30-day PSN social features ban for sending my friend a photo of the nudist colony in GTA6 that I found.".

In a recent development, in a screenshot of the notice, PlayStation Safety states that content sent from the player's account via Message on PlayStation "breached the Code of Conduct", and that their account has been "temporarily suspended from using PlayStation social features for 30 days" due to "pornographic or obscene content". It also warns that "further offenses may result in temporary or permanent suspension from the whole of PlayStation, not just social features".

PlayStation's Code of Conduct asks players not to "share, solicit, access, distribute or store material that is obscene, pornographic or illegal", and indicates Sony "may take any action as reasonably necessary to protect PlayStation and our players".

Sources indicate that DO NOT, I REPEAT DO NOT SEND ANY PHOTOS TAKEN WITH THE IN GAME CAMERA , ACROSS THE PSN MESSAGING NETWORK THAT CONTAIN NUDITY. I JUST GOT A 30 DAY PSN SOCIAL FEATURES BAN FOR SENDING MY FRIEND A PHOTO OF THE NUDIST COLONY IN GTA6 THAT I FOUND. pic.twitter.com/vsoIjmpGrt.

Industry observers note that crucially, as Dexerto points out, the code does not make an exception for content taken from games, even ones rated for adults. So if you've snapped anything cheeky in Leonida - say, full-frontal nudity in its nudist resort - you might want to keep it to yourself.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that exoprimal, Capcom's 2023 team shooter pitting exosuited fighters against T-rexes, is the latest game to be handed an expiration date.
  • Capcom announced as much in a post running through all of the permutations of the shutdown, which is coming on September 29th 2027 at 8AM PDT.
  • The publishers have already stopped selling Exoprimal's seasonal survival passes, with plans to pull the game itself and all DLC from sale as of March 30th 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that exoprimal, Capcom's 2023 team shooter pitting exosuited fighters against T-rexes, is the latest game to be handed an expiration date. Its online services will cease as of late September 2027, rendering it unplayable, with the game set to be delisted from stores in March.

Capcom announced as much in a post running through all of the permutations of the shutdown, which is coming on September 29th 2027 at 8AM PDT. "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement," they wrote.

The publishers have already stopped selling Exoprimal's seasonal survival passes, with plans to pull the game itself and all DLC from sale as of March 30th 2027. Those who already own Exoprimal will be able to re-download it in the time between it being pulled from stores and the server shutdown in September, meaning there's plenty of time to hop in for a final few rounds of dino shooting if you fancy.

Recent findings suggest that it's long seemed like only a matter of time before the dino shooter was taken offline, with Capcom having stopped releasing new seasonal additions to it all the way back in July 2024. So, this seems more like a natiral petering out than an instance of an online game being cut down in its prime or not long after launch, as we've seen recently with extreme cases like Highguard. As such, one would hope there's a chance plenty of Exoprimal devs have already been redirected onto other Capcom games, minimising the amount who might be left in the often precarious position of having nothing immediate to work on following this shutdown.

It's fair to say Ed Thorn (RPS in peace) wasn't a fan of Exoprimal on reviewing it at launch. "I thought Exoprimal somehow managed to make dinosaurs versus mechs, aka the coolest concept ever, boring in my review-in-progress,"he wrote. "I held out hope it would improve, though, as lots of commenters assured me it's fun side would finally surface. "Just play several more hours and things really open up! Variety in the dinos, in the modes, in just about everything!". To some extent, they were right. There are fun moments to be had as you queue up for Dino Survival and suddenly, remarkably, things have changed a bit.

It has been revealed that "But the game doesn't respect your time. It forces you to sit through hours of repetitive dino-slaying and then only offers you the chance, the chance to slay dinos in a way that isn't excruciatingly samey. Even as someone who finds the fun in mindless carnage, I'd much rather ditch my mech suit and let the dinosaurs run rampant. The dinosaurs don't deserve this.".

That's not exactly as positive a eulogy as the one offered by Capcom, but not all games are destined to stick the landing and be universally beloved mega-hits, especially those wading into the live service maelstrom.

It's been a full week since GTA 6 released, if you can believe it. After years and years and years of waiting for it to finally arrive, I hope that you've been enjoying your life in Leonida.

I say that because it's quite obviously time to rate the game for yourself.

To recap, GTA 6 remains the highest rated title ever released. It now has over 160 reviews on Metacritic and it still sits at a frankly staggering 99 score. It's extremely difficult to imagine that it'll ever be equalled — never mind beaten.

Recent findings suggest that but it hasn't all been smooth sailing for Rockstar's latest. The game's been review bombed for a variety of reasons by frustrated people — once again sparking conversations surrounding the legitimacy of user reviews in general.

Counter to that, it's worth noting that GTA 6 is exceptionally highly rated on the PS Store, where people actually have to buy the game before giving it a score out of five. 389,000 ratings and it's at 4.78 — which equates to 92% of players giving it a full five stars.

Recent findings suggest that you don't have to agree with all the praise, though — that's what these polls are for. Maybe you like GTA 6 but still think that it's overrated, or perhaps it's struggling to live up to your lofty expectations.

Our view is simple enough: Push Square editor Sammy dubbed it "the greatest open world game ever made" in his GTA 6 PS5 review, awarding the title a very rare 10/10.

"Rockstar has set a new sandbox standard here, with a world that feels alive and populated with real people; Leonida is a place where it appears almost anything can happen at any time," he wrote — and I don't think he's wrong!

Sources indicate that but would you agree? Is GTA 6 truly deserving of all those 10/10 review scores? It's time to have your say in our poll, before attempting to explain yourself in the comments section below.

Please note voting will score the game in your games collection.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • PS5 players averaged 513 minutes in GTA 6 that day, which is over eight and a half hours, while Xbox players averaged 494 minutes, or around eight and a quarter hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day, more than half of everyone playing on PS5 and Xbox was playing GTA 6.

Citing latest data from Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, analyst Mat Piscatella stated on Bluesky that 61 percent of US PlayStation 5 players and 56 percent of global Xbox players who were active on 19th November "engaged with Grand Theft Auto 6".

PS5 players averaged 513 minutes in GTA 6 that day, which is over eight and a half hours, while Xbox players averaged 494 minutes, or around eight and a quarter hours.

"Both the DAU [daily active users] and minutes played engagement rates are absolutely bonkers," Piscatella wrote.

For comparison, Fortnite had the second-highest engagement rate that day, with 10 percent of active players across both platforms playing it.

Piscatella also shared the top five games that GTA 6 players had been playing in the two weeks before launch, between 6th and 19th November: Fortnite, Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto 5 (Remastered), Roblox, and NBA 2K27.

According to Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, Grand Theft Auto VI had a massive launch (surprise!).For players active on November 19th, 61% of US PlayStation 5 and 56% of global Xbox players engaged with Grand Theft Auto VI.PS5 GTA VI players averaged 513 minutes that day, Xbox players 494.

The figures come after Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 had become the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day.

GTA 6 rolled out on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's one of the best-reviewed games of all time, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, with plenty of comedy on the 2026 Netflix streaming schedule, I've always appreciated how John Mulaney can take something ordinary and turn it into an absurdly funny story. Whether he's talking about taking his Korean in-laws to CVS, his children saying scary things, or any number of his hilarious stand-up jokes, his delivery makes even the most ridiculous observations sound perfectly reasonable. Although apparently, one fast-food joke didn't survive the trip from the comedy club to one of his specials, and the reason is pretty hilarious.

The story comes courtesy of filmmaker Cairo Smith, who shared an anecdote on X about attending an early test performance of one of Mulaney's stand-up specials. According to Smith, the comedian had been working on a bit about Yoshinoya Beef Bowl, the Japanese fast-food chain known for its rice bowls. Smith writes in his post, as you can see below, that when the comedian asked audiences who'd been to the establishment, a shocking number had, derailing the entire premise.

According to recent reports, one time I went to see an early test performance of a John Mulaney special at a comedy club in LA. And he had a joke about Yoshinoya beef bowl where the joke was that nobody goes there. So he asked the audience, like, who here has actually been to Yoshinoya Beef Bowl? And like a shocking amount of people raised their hands and cheered, like so many that he didn't even know how to continue the bit and just moved on. And then when the special came out, pretty much everything was the same but the Yoshinoya beef bowl bit was gone. And now for some reason that's one of the only John Mulaney bits I can remember.November 24, 2026.

According to Smith, the response left Mulaney unsure how to continue, so he simply moved on to his next bit. I have to assume that's not how the comedian was expecting things to god own.

When the finished special eventually premiered, Smith noticed that the Yoshinoya material had disappeared, even though it was the only bit of material they could remember. Considering how many great John Mulaney comedy specials we've gotten over the years, I can't help wondering how many other jokes disappeared during those early performances.

Recent findings suggest that I think the audience unintentionally created a funnier moment than whatever Mulaney originally had planned. There's something wonderful about a comedian confidently walking into a punchline only to discover that everybody in the room has apparently been eating at the restaurant he's mocking. And it seems Mulaney remembers the experience.

Responding to the story on X, Mulaney acknowledged the memory and revealed that he'd encountered a similar problem while testing a recent joke, writing:.

Sources indicate that l remember this well. The same thing happened in September with a bit I tried about Orange Julius.

I'd love to know exactly what he was planning to say about Orange Julius, because that's another restaurant chain that feels tailor-made for a Mulaney routine. The Yoshinoya detail actually sent me down a bit of a rabbit hole because this isn't the first time the restaurant has figured into one of Mulaney's jokes.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

In a recent development, fans of Saturday Night Live might remember Bill Hader's hilarious return as Stefon in 2018, during which Mulaney appeared as the character's attorney, Shy. At one point, he leaned over to whisper something into Hader's ear. Whatever he said caused Hader to completely lose his composure. Of course, Hader has a long history of losing it during Stefon appearances, and his inability to keep a straight face has produced some of SNL's funniest unplanned moments.

During a subsequent appearance on Late Night With Seth Meyers, Hader revealed that Mulaney had whispered a completely unexpected line about his girlfriend working at Yoshinoya Beef Bowl. It's such an oddly specific thing to say that I can understand why Hader couldn't keep a straight face. Mulaney has a knack for finding humor in names and places that most of us probably wouldn't think twice about.

Mulaney has certainly had plenty of success with the jokes that survived that process. Between his stand-up specials, his work on SNL and his surprisingly personal Netflix series Everybody's Live With John Mulaney, he's established himself as one of the most recognizable comedians working today.

Still, I have to admit that I'd happily watch an entire special made up of the jokes that didn't make the final cut. Especially if they're accompanied by stories about exactly how they fell apart. But for now, I'll happily revisit his prior specials and Everybody's Live with my Netflix subscription.

Ryan graduated from Missouri State University with a BA in English/Creative Writing. An expert in all things horror, Ryan enjoys covering a wide variety of topics. He's also a lifelong comic book fan and an avid watcher of Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nicalis has removed AI-generated music from The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ after players discovered it in the game's latest update, prompting a wave of negative reviews on Steam.

The music in question was tied to a run themed around Grand Theft Auto 6, which launched on the same day (19th November). A day later, Reddit user ShweetsStuff posted that the run's music was "100% generated by Suno (AI) (with proof)", pointing to tracks that reference the AI music tool Suno in their metadata.

"Thanks, Nicalis, for breaking everything and adding AI slop to an already-existing game!" one Steam review reads (thanks, IGN).

"I'm starting to think that adding AI to a game should be valid grounds [for] refunds to people who have already paid for and played a game," said another.

Woke up to a shit show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.

Responding to the criticism, Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen remarked he "woke up to a shit show".

"Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned," he wrote on X/Twitter, before inviting players to report challenges and bugs to the email address shared in one of Nicalis' tweets, which confirmed it had "pushed a newly introduced build with critical fixes", including the "removal of generated music files". The patch is live on PC, and Nicalis claims it has been submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo, and Sony.

Nicalis has yet to explain how the music ended up in the game.

Hi All!Repentance+ Upgrade:The team has pushed a upcoming build with critical fixes.• Removal of generated music files• Larynx + Car Battery Bug Fix• PC patch—should be live already• Submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo and Sony ASAPAdditional: • Continuing work on netcode… pic.twitter.com/d1gyLUlBK8.

Following the gigantic Afterbirth and Afterbirth+ expansions, released in 2015 and 2017 respectively, The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth grew again with 2021's community-inspired, sequel-sized Repentance DLC. That was meant to be the last content drop for real, yet 2024 gave us the free Repentance+ DLC, which finally added online co-op to the disturbingly charming roguelike. The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth has since hit a fresh concurrent player record on Steam 12 years after it was released.

McMillen's most recent game, Mewgenics, also made quite a splash earlier this year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've lost count of how many times I've settled down to play a brand-newly introduced game on Steam, only to be smacked in the face with a giant popup telling me to "Grab a controller and kick back!" instead of using my humble mouse and keyboard.

Recent findings suggest that thankfully for me I live in a multi-platform household, meaning a controller is never far out of reach. But I've also got staunch PC pals without a pad to pick up and who, rightly enough, don't want to fork out the kinda cash that PlayStation's DualSense or the Xbox controller require.

But I'm a firm believer that a good controller is a must-have tool in a PC gamer's repertoire these days, and we needn't immediately seek out the big names when it comes to a comfortable, robust gamepad. Tons of budget-friendly options have popped up on the market over the years, and while some of them are admittedly pretty naff there are also a bunch of great controllers that won't break the bank.

In fact, I've got three of 'em for under $25 for you right here. That's a third of the price of a DualSense controller! While they don't come with fancy haptics and adaptive triggers, they do offer stick-drift resistant, low-latency gaming. Which, as fun as the bells as whistles can be, are really the most vital bits.

A upcoming and improved version of the original Nova Lite, the Nova Lite 2 has Hall effect everything, 1000 Hz polling, and trigger locks. It even has a mechanical D-pad, which is absurd for the money, really.

Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect.

Price check: Amazon $29.99 (Grey).

In a recent development, out of the three choices, our pad professional James Bentley tells me he likes the GameSir Nova Lite 2 the best, right now going for $23 at Walmart. It boasts comfort, decent polling, and Hall effect—so much better protection against that pesky stick drift. It's also got our highest review score out of the bunch thanks to its affordability, mechanical d-pad, and choice of 2.4Ghz and Bluetooth.

It's not got great grip, however, and its budget is felt in the less-than-stellar plastic and rather simple software. But for the price you're paying? It's a great, basic choice for those who only need to reach for a controller occasionally.

According to recent reports, we've already raved about Hall effect joysticks and how they spell the end for the dreaded stick drift. In this wireless gaming controller, they're a welcome feature, but this handful of gaming hardware packs a few quirky surprises too. For instance, there are extra bumper buttons.

Key specs: Hall effect sticks, triggers | 2.4G wireless | 19 h battery.

Price check: Best Buy $21.99 (Black) | Walmart $29.99 (Purple).

It has been revealed that but if you're someone who's accustomed to the likes of the Switch Pro controller, you might find the 8BitDo Ultimate 2C a better fit, right now going for $20 at Amazon. It's got a pretty similar shape, and also sports those beloved Hall effect joysticks. It does have a little bit of a mushy d-pad but hey, look at that lovely colourway!

Sources indicate that finally, if you're looking to spend as little as possible, the GameSir Nova Lite comes in as the cheapest option at a mere $18. It's got less mappable buttons than its successor thanks to no back paddles, and is overall a downgrade. For the extra four bucks I'd personally just go for the newer version, but if you're really looking to really squeeze every cent, it's certainly an option worth considering.

According to recent reports, it's incredible to think you can spend so little and get a stick drift-resistant wireless controller that doesn't completely suck. Luckily for the GameSir Nova Lite, it does all of the above and manages to feel good and light in the hands, too.

Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect.
