Latest Update: 12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1033 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that in a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it.
  • You can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex.
  • If Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it. You get to enjoy all the brightly colored lights your neighbors put up, but you don’t have to put up your own. You don’t have to do any duty-shopping. There's no pressure. But Christmas Day itself leaves you in a mostly shuttered world that feels like there’s nothing going on. Fortunately, there are options to make Dec. 25 a fun day off, regardless of your observances.

You can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex. Chinese restaurants and movie theaters traditionally stay open on Christmas Day for those who don't celebrate, and they’re often filled with fellow Christmas refugees. Check Google for the hours of your local Chinese restaurant and give them a call to make a reservation. If you’re more adventurous and you’re in a city large enough to have a Chinatown (or a whatever-town), just head straight there on Christmas and see what happens—that’s how the best days usually start.

If Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses. Just make sure you check first. Lots of chain restaurants are open on Christmas Day too, including Applebee's, McDonald’s, Benihana, and more. You can even get Christmas breakfast at your local IHOP. But not every location of every outlet follows the same hours.

In a recent development, as for movies, most chain multiplex theaters are open on Dec. 25, and theaters are usually pretty full. The movies attract both people who don't celebrate Christmas and people who do, but want to get away from their families for a couple hours, so make sure and reserve a seat beforehand. Consider hitting up an out-of-the-way spot or that theater with the table service and cushy recliners to make it feel like more of an occasion.

Industry observers note that most people going to the movies on Christmas Day aren’t there for Christmas movies, so interesting “secular” movies are often slated for release on the 25th. This year's Christmas is unusually packed with interesting latest movies, including family flick Jumani: Open World, a Robert Eggers horror movie called Werwulf, and the crowd pleasing football story Mr. Irrelevant, so you have serious options.

Recent findings suggest that chinese restaurants and movie theaters aren’t the only establishments open on Christmas. Here are some other options:.

In a recent development, go skiing or snowboarding: Most mountains are open on Christmas, and the lift lines are blissfully empty. There's no better way of celebrating a winter-based holiday than on a wide-open mountain.

Visit a skating rink: Speaking of winter sports, ice skating rinks are generally open on Christmas too.

Pretend to be a tourist: Tourist attractions are often open on Christmas, especially in larger cities. This includes places like Madame Tussaud’s and Ripley’s Believe It or Not, as well as ziplines and Segway tours—so do that touristy thing you’ve never done before.

In a recent development, get a room: If you’ve got some spare cash and have nothing better to do, get a room at a hotel. Hotels don’t usually close on Christmas, and they typically offer plenty of amenities, so take advantage of the pool at the Holiday Inn or the spa at the Four Seasons, depending on your lifestyle.

Hiking and biking: Hiking trails and parks are open on Christmas if you want to get outdoors. If you’re into biking, hit the trails or hit the streets: Traffic is minimal on Christmas, so it’s a great time to put in some serious roadwork.

Volunteer: Not having anything to do on Christmas isn’t the biggest life problem, especially compared to people who have nowhere to go and nothing to eat. So use Christmas to help people and actually deliver on that whole “good will towards men” thing. Check your local Craigslist for volunteering opportunities.

Use Christmas as a catch-up day: This is strictly for type-A people, but if everyone is out of town and no one is going to call you, why not spend the day catching up on neglected chores or personal projects? You can spend at least part of your day knocking a few things off your to-do list and the rest of the time relaxing. That way you’ll get a break and still feel accomplished.

Just sleep all day: Type-B personalities like me see a day free of obligations and other people as a golden opportunity to do as little as is humanly possible, a day to fully commit to sloth.

Spend time with friends and family at home: Not celebrating Christmas doesn’t mean you can’t spend the day with family and/or friends. Get together with your loved ones, play games, watch a movie, cook together, talk, or whatever else you all enjoy. You don’t have to go out to have fun, so don’t rule out staying in with people you care about.

Shopping: This is at the bottom of the list because it’s iffy. Drug stores and convenience stores like 711 are usually open on the 25th. Grocery chains like Kroger’s and Trader Joe’s usually aren’t. Your local shopping mall or retail district might be open, but probably won't be, so check ahead.

Because so many places are closed on Christmas Day, you should initiative ahead (unless you like spontaneity and are OK with the possibility of disappointment) by:.

Making a list of the places you want to go.

Calling nearby locations to confirm they’ll be open, as not every chain follows corporate holiday hour recommendations.

Making reservations at any restaurant(s) you plan to visit.

Putting together a basic timeline of the day, accounting for travel time, so you don’t lose any reservations, miss a movie, or arrive after the store closes.

It has been revealed that the most notable advice here is to do something intentional on Christmas, even if it's sleeping in, so the day doesn't feel depressing or empty. So hit the slopes, suck down some dim sum, or keep your couch from floating away, but be sure you make Christmas your own.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, yesterday I made a significant error in judgement. In writing an apology to our readers, I made a target of one of our writers and I won't be able to undo that. What I can try to do is apologise to that writer, who I'm addressing now.

My failures towards you were several. Firstly, in not explaining that we are able to step in by replying to and moderating comments when a discussion is becoming heated or aggressive, I never made it clear there were protections available to you that you weren't receiving.

It has been revealed that secondly, for mentioning you at all in the apology. While I hoped to make it clear to readers we wouldn't disrespect them in future, I laid the blame for that on your feet in public. The responsibility of an editor is to protect their writers, and I failed you profoundly.

In a recent development, thirdly, that I didn't speak to you ahead of the post. As far as you were concerned the matter was settled, and I then put it in public without any warning.

In a recent development, fourth, while we often talk of RPS being a collection of different writers with different viewpoints, where no one member of the team has the definitive view on a subject, this creates a vacuum for our contributors to operate in. This means new writers have very little direction when it comes to how they approach any topic and the response their work may receive. Again, any failings here are ultimately my responsibility.

Finally, this failure is all the more significant because it has happened across lines of gender privilege. RPS has a full-time staff of cisgender men, which inevitably gives rise to bias and ignorance we must actively confront, while we work towards being in a position to address our lack of gender diversity, beyond commissioning the occasional marginalised freelance writer. Non-cisgender writers are both much more exposed to abuse and much less favoured in terms of steady work. As such, a public rebuke from your own editor is far more damaging than it would be if the freelancer were a cisgender man. On this count, I have been extremely thoughtless in ways that would likely not have been the case when this site had a majority female editorship.

Ashley, I am deeply sorry that I let you down in these ways.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • During the original version, Hanks, Moynihan and Day all apparently froze in really exaggerated and over the top poses.
  • Here’s how Moynihan described the conversation he had with Hanks after dress rehearsal to Mashable….
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that SNL surprised fans earlier this season with a David S Pumpkins sketch to celebrate the off-beat spooky character’s tenth anniversary. Current cast member Mikey Day was joined by his OG co-stars Tom Hanks and Bobby Moynihan for what hilariously turned out to be several minutes of freezing in place while James Austin Johnson paused the sketch for his President Trump impression. The bit went over very well with fans at home, but it turns out the broadcast version contained a key change suggested by Tom Hanks who was looking out for everyone’s bodies.

During the original version, Hanks, Moynihan and Day all apparently froze in really exaggerated and over the top poses. Unfortunately for them, they didn’t realize that Johnson’s part with Trump was going to go on for so long. He ultimately talked for four minutes, which left the Pumpkins trio gassed by the time they had to unfreeze and act again. So, Hanks suggested they make a change before the live show.

Here’s how Moynihan described the conversation he had with Hanks after dress rehearsal to Mashable….

In between dress and air, Tom came over to me and was like, ‘Hey, so, we’re all going to close our mouths.’ We were all doing our poses for dress, and on air, we’re just (standing there with our arms folded). We knew we had to stand there for the whole sketch. Tom Hanks is a good actor. He knew (we should) keep our mouths shut, keep our arms down. You don’t want to hold them up for the whole seven minutes of the cold open.

Moynihan stated they probably would have figured all of this out before dress rehearsal, but they actually weren't paying much attention to the larger sketch. Instead, they spent like an hour talking about how absolutely absurd they felt being back in the costumes David S Pumpkins and the Skeletons, who have their own wild names. None of them ever thought the original sketch was going to hit, let alone lead to a TV special and an anniversary sketch a decade later.

You can watch the sketch in its entirety below….

That’s the power of SNL though. Some of the sketches that go viral and live on in people’s memories involve sharp political commentary or really thoughtful parodies of society. Others just involve a goofy character or characters that connect with people for whatever reason. David S Pumpkins and the Skeletons are definitely examples of those characters. They’re just so over the top and ridiculous that you can’t look away, even if they’re frozen in the background of a President Trump sketch and trying to stay as still as possible.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alan Wake and Control studio Remedy Entertainment is right now developing a highly-anticipated Max Payne 1 & 2 remake.

  • Gaudechon is so positive on Remedy's working relationship with Rockstar that he emphasised his praise for Rockstar further.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alan Wake and Control studio Remedy Entertainment is right now developing a highly-anticipated Max Payne 1 & 2 remake. The Finnish studio is doing so in partnership with Grand Theft Auto 6 studio Rockstar, which owns the IP and is funding the remake's development.

According to recent reports, so how has that relationship been? According to Remedy CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon, working with Rockstar has been "amazing". "Honestly, it's been great," Gaudechon told Game File. "You know why? Because I think they're super respectful of Remedy.".

Gaudechon is so positive on Remedy's working relationship with Rockstar that he emphasised his praise for Rockstar further. "I'll say it out loud: They've honestly been an awesome partner. And it's no bullshit," he added.

The original Max Payne was released in 2001, and its sequel in 2003 - both developed by Remedy. Rockstar published the second game and worked on the original's console ports. Rockstar developed a third entry in the series, Max Payne 3, which Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser recently called something of a failure.

"Some people liked it; lots didn't. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success," said Houser.

The Max Payne 1 & 2 remake has been in the works since 2022, but only entered full production in 2024. The game is understood to be Remedy's current project, though the studio also has another unannounced project in the works.

In other Remedy news, the studio recently posted one of its best financial quarters, off the back of the release of Control Resonant, the studio's fastest-selling game ever.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the potentially historic vote at GTA 6 creators Rockstar Games on whether to seek formal union recognition has failed, the International Workers of Great Britain have confirmed. Around 1600 studio members cast ballots across 12th to 26th November, even as the organization's open world Bonnie & Clyde 'em up released onto PlayStation and Xbox storefronts. In the end, approximately 25% of the participants voted in favour.

According to the IWGB themselves, "the result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organising with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives.".

Speaking to RPS in an emailed statement, Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe argued that the vote's failure "reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong." The IWGB, meanwhile, have declared that "this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for". They're going to keep mobilising for more labour power, with the failed vote now framed as a foot in the door.

In a recent development, "Whilst we haven't emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for fresh kinds of conversation to start happening," reads the union statement. "People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We head from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions will lead us.

"A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy," they continue. "But it's one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We'll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.".

According to recent reports, the Rockstar UK unionisation drive has been a long journey. The vote follows open confrontation between Rockstar management in the UK and IWGB-affiliated Rockstar employees working out of a private Discord server. After allegedly keeping the Discord server under surveillance for over two years, Rockstar bosses fired around 30 staff in October 2026 on charges of "gross misconduct" and breach of confidentiality. The IWGB and the fired workers have countered by accusing Rockstar of union-busting, observing that the Discord's putative union membership had reached the 10% minimum required for statutory recognition under UK law, shortly before the firings.

220 Rockstar staff subsequently signed an open letter to management calling for the reinstatement of the fired workers. The IWGB also organised protest rallies outside the offices of Rockstar North in Edinburgh and Take-Two Interactive in London. A UK Member of Parliament weighed in, calling on ministers to "stop this from happening again". Finally, the ousted workers took Rockstar to court in an employment tribunal that has run for much of this year: the closing statements landed on the eve of GTA 6's release, with a judge's verdict pending.

I'm sorry to see the union vote fall through, given the boost a formally recognised GTA developer union in the UK would have given to labour organisation across the industry. In the short term, of course, it might have made for a safer and more supportive workplace at Rockstar. While there is relatively little recent reporting on current working conditions, many Rockstar games are allegedly the product of "crunch culture", stemming back to the development of the first 3D Grand Theft Autos on PS2.

In January 2010, an anonymous user posting on behalf of the “wives of Rockstar San Diego employees" claimed that staff had been forced to work 12-hour, six day weeks to finish the first Red Dead Redemption. A landmark report from Kotaku in 2018, based on interviews with 34 current and 43 former employees, described developers piling up evening and weekend work across Rockstar's empire, with crunch especially severe among QA staff at Rockstar Lincoln in the UK.

Some of Kotaku's sources mentioned they had been explicitly pushed to work overtime by managers, facilitated by workplace systems such as hour-logging. Others spoke of a more vaporous expectation that they put in inhuman effort, because after all, working at the studio behind GTA is a privilege. Many had fond memories of their experiences, even as they acknowledged the toll taken on their minds, bodies and relationships outside work. This is part of the problem with crunch - it doesn't have to be explicitly imposed. It comes about because some creative and enthusiastic people are not good at recognising their own limits, and less scrupulous employers are happy to profit from this and, worse, erect a working culture around it.

The 2018 Kotaku piece acknowledges that some crunch results from the uneven and unpredictable way many videogames are made, but it also talks about overtime brought on by unaccountable leadership, with studio co-founders Dan and Sam Houser "renowned for rebooting, overhauling, and discarding large chunks of their games." (Dan Houser left the firm in 2020.) The same heads were also stated to value the "appearance" of developers going the extra mile, with one dev telling the site they were encouraged to walk a lap of the office on Saturday, whenever the Housers were in town. Together with anxieties about confidentiality, that emphasis on devs being visibly busy perhaps informs Rockstar's cancelling of hybrid working in early 2024, which precipitated some of this year's union activism.

According to recent reports, many of the people pushing for unionisation at Rockstar are also reacting to events across the games industry. There has been a huge wave of mass layoffs as companies "adjust" following the boom period initiated by Covid lockdowns. Some of those laid off had recently shipped commercially successful games, like Battlefield 6. GTA 6 developers have publicly expressed concerns about getting cut, even as their latest open worlder makes sales records.

A chunk of the recent mass layoffs are owing to lucrative manufacturer acquisitions and consolidations that have attracted criticism from existing unions. Microsoft have spent two years axing studios, projects and jobs after spending around $69 billion to acquire Activision Blizzard. EA are now owned by a consortium led by Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund and Donald Trump's son-in-law; the company has since laid off hundreds of developers and closed the mighty BioWare as they shoulder an enormous debt, which they're reportedly hoping to offset by means of mass generative AI-powered costcutting. As alluded to in today's IWGB statement, there is the overarching question of how genAI - often explicitly mandated by executives - will threaten livelihoods by automating tasks, giving bosses an excuse to keep headcounts small by one means or another.

The repeated layoff waves have inspired a lot of union action at many large videogame companies, from Microsoft to Ubisoft, but I suspect a lot of that hasn't been apparent outside labour organising and enthusiast circles. GTA is as breakthrough a vidya as you can get. Rockstar forming a union would have been a foundation from which to talk more about worker power beyond the games industry.

It has been revealed that as often when reporting on unionisation, I'm left idly wondering about what kind of art a fully unionised industry would create. The production conditions of many games can be deduced from their design – a photorealistic open world game, for example, is a vast assemblage of resources that may hinge on distributed development across an unequal world. Rockstar both represent AAA gaming at its grAAAndest, and have historically been part of the auteur craze, with the Housers having the final say on every detail.

We are, in general, all very familiar with the caricatures of auteur-led development, positioned as a source of both eccentric brilliance and ruinous hubris. I think there's much less of a narrative for the kind of art you get from teams where workers have serious negotiating power, though there are precedents in the form of cooperatives and similar organisations that tether their labour conditions more boldly to the kind of art they produce: for example, Die Gute Fabrik, and most recently, Summer Eternal.

It has been revealed that A unionised Rockstar wouldn't just be a space in which workers are better protected against the expectations of managers and financial stakeholders; you'd get different kinds of art. Maybe more interesting kinds of art! I do wonder if union organisers could do a more effective job of expressing this hope, perhaps exploring where certain games have lost their way because workers were treated like cannon fodder.

A post shared by 1- UP Gaming (@1upgaming03).

Industry observers note that in a video posted to Instagram, for instance, we see a player casually walking into a jewelry store with a crate of beer under one arm and a swift right hook ready to go in the other. That's when Jason goes on a throwing spree, knocking out staff with some well-placed projectiles to the head and dusting up those who get a little close. Aside from a very brief alarm from a locked door, the robbery goes smoothly.

A post shared by Kotov GTA6 стримы (@kotov.plays).

A faster, less flash example shows a quick and easy shop robbery where a casual bottle to the bloke behind the counter allows for rapid access to the cash in the till. Whether bottles can be utilised for something more complicated, like a full-on bank heist, remains to be seen.

Industry observers note that bottles, though, are just the tip of the iceberg. Roadkill and random lizards on the street also make for handy non-lethal projectiles. Beer remains the more compelling option, however. In gun terms, beer crates have up to six rounds in their 'magazine', making them a reliable single source of stuff to throw at folks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's a new survival game blowing up on Steam, and it's not for the faint of heart.

Casualties: Unknown rolled out on November 9 and it's since racked up more than 5,600 user reviews, 98% of which are positive, making it one of the highest-rated newly introduced survival games to hit Steam in some time.

Industry observers note that before you jump in, you should be ready for what sounds like an incredibly punishing, visceral experience built around some very heavy, disturbing themes like drug use, depression, self-harm, and severe mental illness. I remember writing a similar PSA before recommending the 2024 horror gem Mouthwashing, and while I haven't yet gone hands-on with Casualties: Unknown, it definitely sounds like it's in the same wheelhouse thematically.

The game puts you in the shoes (paws?) of a bioengineered, animal-like humanoid whose sole purpose is corporate experimentation, a mission of retrieving lost cargo from a cave system running through a hostile alien world. I already have a profound fear of spelunking, but being forced to do so by an evil corporation with literally zero regard for your well-being is about the most horrific manifestation of that fear I can fathom.

Sources indicate that things are equally, or maybe even more grim, on the gameplay side of things. You platform your way down 11 layers of progressively more dangerous cave systems and fight to avoid losing consciousness. "You will have to bandage yourself, fight infected wounds, and stabilize blood loss before losing consciousness. Additionally, your mood can greatly affect your chances of survival, too much doom and gloom will make your life harder," states developer Orsoniks.

Industry observers note that it sounds a little like the 2017 survival game Rain World, in which you play as a "slugcat" in a dangerous wasteland. Except Casualties: Unknown almost centers around a unique, very gross "simulated limb and cardiovascular system" that requires keeping tabs on things like blood flow and oxygenation, as well as targeted medical intervention. Casualties: Unknown also has more roguelike elements like procedurally generated environments, permadeath, and run resets.

It has been revealed that also similar to Rain World, according to pretty much every Steam review I read, is Casualties: Unknown's extreme difficulty. Orsoniks itself describes the game as "an unforgiving cave-exploration survival simulator" and "a hardcore survival simulation" where "injuries are unavoidable," so you can forget about that no-hit run right now. One reviewer says it's even harder than the 2020 roguelike Noita, yet another notoriously unforgiving game.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Another Steam user lists the number of ways they've died, including: "Sepsis, a pulmonary embolism, a fractured tibia, landmine to the body, spike trap from foot to collar bone, had my jaw ripped off, overdosing, falling from a great height, getting thrown into a ceiling by a jump-mine, depression, drinking bleach accidentally, radiation sickness, normal sickness, poisoning, drowning, hyper and hypothermia, exhaustion, tiredness, blood loss, starvation, thirst, psychotic break, and enemies.".

It has been revealed that again, not for the faint of heart. But if you're the type of video game enjoyer who finds increasing reward proportionate to the level of adversity overcome, Casualties: Unknown seems like quite the value. And with almost 100% positive reviews, it sounds like it's very much worth the pain it inflicts on you.

  • According to recent reports, if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode.
  • In a recent development, your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that you can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely latest side of the game.

According to recent reports, if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

In a recent development, your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

In a recent development, EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

It has been revealed that hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

It has been revealed that if you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

When you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

While driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

Stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

When you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Writing in Alinea's newsletter, Rhys Elliott said Call of Duty HQ's daily active customers (DAUs) across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam fell 42 percent when GTA 6 introduced on 19th November, dropping from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6's launch took a big bite out of Call of Duty’s player base, according to newly introduced estimates from Alinea Analytics, and four days on, it still hasn't recovered.

Writing in Alinea's newsletter, Rhys Elliott said Call of Duty HQ's daily active customers (DAUs) across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam fell 42 percent when GTA 6 introduced on 19th November, dropping from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million. On PlayStation, which Elliott describes as "CoD's main platform", the drop was 44 percent.

In a recent development, "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days," Elliott wrote. "It's still down 41% from its baseline.".

Recent findings suggest that fortnite and FC 27 took a hit too, but both are already recovering. Fortnite's DAUs on PlayStation and Xbox fell 28 percent, from 17.8 million to 12.8 million, but by the end of the weekend it had clawed its way back to 19 percent below its baseline.

Epic is also holding a live event to close out the current season on 5th December, which Elliott says the studio "hopes will pull players back after they’ve polished off GTA 6’s story".

FC 27's DAUs dropped by around 27 percent, from 5.9 million to 4.3 million, and it's already back within 20 percent of its baseline.

It has been revealed that GTA 6's launch hit Call of Duty HARD (@alineaanalytics estimates).COD HQ's daily active consumers across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam are down 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M. On PlayStation – CoD’s main platform – Call of Duty took a 44% hit. Sadly, CoD has barely bounced… pic.twitter.com/XLa6N9TBfr.

According to Alinea, of those who'd played GTA 6 by the end of its launch weekend, 29 percent had also played Fortnite this month, 16 percent had played Call of Duty HQ, and 11 percent had played FC 27.

In a recent development, elliott remarked the pattern is largely what Alinea had predicted: the massive live service games took an instant hit from GTA, but bounced back "because they're ingrained habits". Call of Duty is "the outlier here", he added, "and Xbox should - candidly - be worried about one of its premier franchises".

Elliott also points out that all of this is the impact of GTA 6's single-player mode. He expects its online component and PC port to arrive "some time next year", and when they do, he says, "the bounce back will not be so obtainable".

Alinea also estimates that GTA 6 has sold 44.9 million copies and made more than $4 billion since launch.

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. While it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Aspects of GTA 6 are inspired by Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system because its player agency 'was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from'

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just mark a huge, and at times unbelievable, step forward for graphics; it's also at the forefront of what an open world game can be, just look at the existential crisis it's given Cyberpunk 2's creative director. With thousands of enterable buildings, unpredictable and slightly scary NPCs, and systems that help you determine what kind of criminal you want to be. It all really does feel like a milestone for what videogames can do.

"As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, claims in an interview with Eurogamer. "So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun.".

It has been revealed that the sophisticated mechanics that Nelson is talking about here pertains to GTA 6's Criminal Profile, a system that evaluates your escapades across Leonida and gives you a rating. There's Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable. The more stealthy and non-lethal you are, the higher your profile will be. It's similar to Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor System.

It has been revealed that "There was maybe more emotional resonance in the story of RDR2 than we had, certainly in a GTA before," Nelson says. "So we liked that idea. We didn't necessarily come to GTA 6 going: 'We must have emotional resonance,' but all of those things combine. It's more that those systems and that element of player choice and agency, and the way that affected the narrative, was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from.".

Recent findings suggest that nelson explains that most of the groundwork started as "simple things" in principle, "but they create a lot more work in terms of development of the sophistication of the systems." It's all about choice in GTA 6. You choose whether you want to be a criminal with a conscience or a loose cannon.

"It's still a world of violence, but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don't have to beat them to death to get their money.".

The part that sticks out the most is that you "don't have to" approach crimes in a certain way, there's still the option to go into every encounter guns blazing because redemption only works from a storytelling perspective when it's the player's choice, and not as Nelson puts it, something that is "foisted upon you".

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"You can still go on those rampages and basically smash your Criminal Profile until it breaks," Nelson adds. "And then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically says, 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'".

Am I brave enough to reject the criminal profile system entirely? Hell no. I replay sections of dialogue if I accidentally upset someone, and cannot do an "evil run" of a game without giving myself stomach ulcers because of the guilt—but I appreciate having the option.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Witcher 3 Remastered continues to recieve tweaks ahead of the Songs of the Past expansion arriving next year to whisk Gerry from the River off on a fresh adventure. Following some bloomin' improvements in October, its latest patch does a bunch of skill and mutation balancing, alongside further technical tweaks and fixes for some funky bugs.

Sources indicate that "Fixed an issue where Reforging the Mastercrafted or Grandmaster Feline armor gave Geralt an unusual hairstyle," reads the first of numerous notes in the visual section of patch 5.02's notes about weird stuff happening to Gerry's luscious mane. "Fixed an issue where Geralt could become bald after enabling HairWorks on PC or Xbox Play Anywhere and then continuing the game on Xbox via Cross Progression," reads another that sounds slightly more serious. "Fixed an issue where growing a beard with the Rabble-rouser hairstyle made Geralt's head invisible," reads a third, which takes the cake.

According to recent reports, there've also been instances of Gerry or NPCs missing their faces or "other body parts". The NPCs, bless them, have also had to deal with contracting "overly bright red areas on their legs" when moving through crowds. Oh, and a building near Novigrad's docks has been cheeklily disappearing whenever Geralt gets close to it. One would assume it's just a bit shy, though that's a tough thing to be when your location means people embarking and disembarking from ships are constantly walking past. To be honest, it also sounds like it could have been adapted into an extra contract for Gerry if CD Projekt had fancied. The studio have also "fixed an glitch where installing and uninstalling mods could cause merchants' inventories, Geralt's inventory and storage to be emptied".

Recent findings suggest that beyond the giggle-worthy bug fixes, the most consequential aspect of the patch to my eye will likely be the tweaks to the power of certain skills and mutations, which folks may well be testing out if they're trying to settle on a fresh build before Songs of the Past. Those tweaks are as follows:.

Sources indicate that generally speaking, sign-heavy Gerry builds look like they'll be most acutely affected and be less effective following this patch. I typically only rely on Quen for a bit of shielding, because I'm an unimaginative monster slayer, so I'm not sure I'll notice it too much, but if you really make the most of your magical abilities it might hit your Gerry pretty hard.

Sources indicate that it's worth skimming through the full notes if you've time, which also contain a few PC-specific fixes and tweaks. Starting a Hearts of Stone or Blood and Wine-only playthrough on Steam Deck should no longer lead to long load times, for example, while there've been some improvements made to path tracing and ray reconstruction .
